How to memorise with this book

  1. Learn (once). Read Spot it, say the hook out loud, read the code with the highlighted lines, then type it on LeetCode from memory and submit. Tick learn.
  2. Review (on the printed dates). Cover the code with a sheet of paper. From the title and the hook, write only the highlighted lines on scrap paper. Uncover and compare. Tick the date box.
  3. Variations. After the main code, read each variation and say what changes. The code for each one is printed, so you can check yourself.
  4. Final pass (5 Dec). Only the Recall Sheet at the back. No new problems the day before the exam.

“The hook” one line to say out loud; it is the whole idea.

Day 1

Set up, Java toolkit, fast input

Accounts, the Java collections you will use every day, and how FastScanner replaces Scanner.

plan date Sat 7 Nov
learn these cards Wed 25 Nov
Pattern coreJava toolkit: the lines you type in every problem
LeetCode imports java.util.* for you. In the Infosys editor, write import java.util.*; and import java.io.*; yourself.
static void toolkit(int[] nums, int lo, int hi) {    // HashMap: count, read with a default, group into lists    Map<Integer, Integer> cnt = new HashMap<>();    for (int x : nums) cnt.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);    int seen = cnt.getOrDefault(42, 0);    Map<Integer, List<Integer>> where = new HashMap<>();    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) where.computeIfAbsent(nums[i], k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(i);​    // ArrayDeque: stack = push / pop / peek, queue = offer / poll / peek    Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();    st.push(1); st.peek(); st.pop();    Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();    q.offer(1); q.peek(); q.poll();​    // PriorityQueue: a min-heap unless you pass a comparator    PriorityQueue<Integer> minHeap = new PriorityQueue<>();    PriorityQueue<Integer> maxHeap = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());    PriorityQueue<int[]> byCost = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));​    // TreeMap: sorted keys + neighbour lookups (each returns null when there is none)    TreeMap<Integer, Integer> tm = new TreeMap<>(Map.of(1, 10, 7, 70));    tm.floorKey(5);     // largest key <= 5   -> 1    tm.ceilingKey(5);   // smallest key >= 5  -> 7    tm.lowerKey(5);     // largest key < 5    tm.higherKey(5);    // smallest key > 5    tm.firstKey(); tm.lastKey(); tm.pollFirstEntry();​    // Sorting    int[][] iv = {{3, 4}, {1, 2}};    Arrays.sort(iv, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));   // int[][] by first column    Integer[] boxed = {3, 1, 2};    Arrays.sort(boxed, Collections.reverseOrder());          // descending needs Integer[]    List<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>(List.of(3, 1, 2));    list.sort(Collections.reverseOrder());​    // Strings and overflow guards    char[] cs = "listen".toCharArray();    Arrays.sort(cs);    String key = new String(cs);                             // "eilnst"    StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("ab").reverse();    // "ba"    long safe = (long) Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1;                // cast BEFORE adding    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;                            // never (lo + hi) / 2}
LC 1Two SumEasyDay 1 · #1
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3HashMap · look back
Spot itTwo indices whose values sum to target, array not sorted.
“Ask the map before you tell the map.”
class Solution {    public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {        Map<Integer, Integer> indexOf = new HashMap<>();   // value -> index        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {            Integer j = indexOf.get(target - nums[i]);      // partner seen earlier?            if (j != null) return new int[]{j, i};            indexOf.put(nums[i], i);                        // store AFTER the check        }        return new int[0];    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapCheck target - nums[i] BEFORE storing nums[i], or [3] with target 6 pairs 3 with itself.
Variations
LC 167 · Two Sum II (input is sorted)
Sorted input → two pointers and O(1) space. The answer is 1-indexed.
public int[] twoSum(int[] numbers, int target) {    int l = 0, r = numbers.length - 1;    while (l < r) {        int s = numbers[l] + numbers[r];        if (s == target) return new int[]{l + 1, r + 1};        if (s < target) l++; else r--;      // too small: move left up; too big: move right down    }    return new int[0];}
  • Count pairs with sum k — Same loop: count += seen.getOrDefault(k - x, 0); then seen.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);
  • 3Sum / 4Sum — Sort first and use two pointers instead (Day 3, LC 15).
LC 242Valid AnagramEasyDay 1 · #2
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Counting array
Spot itSame letters, same counts? Only lowercase a–z.
“One string adds, the other subtracts, all zero at the end.”
class Solution {    public boolean isAnagram(String s, String t) {        if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;        int[] cnt = new int[26];        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {            cnt[s.charAt(i) - 'a']++;            cnt[t.charAt(i) - 'a']--;        }        for (int c : cnt) if (c != 0) return false;        return true;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space (26 counters)
TrapDifferent lengths can never be anagrams: return early.
Variations
LC 438 · Find All Anagrams in a String
The same counts, slid along s as a fixed window of length |p|.
public List<Integer> findAnagrams(String s, String p) {    List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();    if (p.length() > s.length()) return res;    int[] need = new int[26], win = new int[26];    for (char c : p.toCharArray()) need[c - 'a']++;    for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {        win[s.charAt(i) - 'a']++;                                // add the new right char        if (i >= p.length()) win[s.charAt(i - p.length()) - 'a']--;   // drop the char that left        if (Arrays.equals(win, need)) res.add(i - p.length() + 1);    }    return res;}
  • LC 383 Ransom Note — Add the magazine, subtract the note; any count below 0 → false.
  • Unicode letters — Use Map<Character, Integer> instead of int[26].
LC 20Valid ParenthesesEasyDay 1 · #3
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Stack
Spot itBrackets must close in the reverse order they opened.
“Push the closer you expect; pop must match.”
class Solution {    public boolean isValid(String s) {        Deque<Character> st = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {            if (c == '(') st.push(')');                     // expect its closer            else if (c == '[') st.push(']');            else if (c == '{') st.push('}');            else if (st.isEmpty() || st.pop() != c) return false;        }        return st.isEmpty();    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapA closer on an empty stack → false. Leftover openers at the end → false.
Variations
LC 32 · Longest Valid Parentheses
Stack of indices with a "base" index: the position just before the current valid run.
public int longestValidParentheses(String s) {    Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();    st.push(-1);                                   // base before index 0    int best = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {        if (s.charAt(i) == '(') st.push(i);        else {            st.pop();            if (st.isEmpty()) st.push(i);          // unmatched ')' becomes the new base            else best = Math.max(best, i - st.peek());        }    }    return best;}
LC 921 · Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
One bracket type → two counters, no stack.
public int minAddToMakeValid(String s) {    int open = 0, add = 0;    for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {        if (c == '(') open++;        else if (open > 0) open--;        else add++;                 // a ')' with nothing to match    }    return add + open;              // plus the '(' never closed}
  • Only ( and ) — No stack needed: keep open; it must never drop below 0 and must end at 0.
LC 347Top K Frequent ElementsMediumDay 1 · #4
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3HashMap + min-heap of size k
Spot itThe k most frequent values.
“Count, then keep a small heap: push, and pop when it grows past k.”
class Solution {    public int[] topKFrequent(int[] nums, int k) {        Map<Integer, Integer> cnt = new HashMap<>();        for (int x : nums) cnt.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);        PriorityQueue<int[]> heap = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1])); // min by count        for (Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e : cnt.entrySet()) {            heap.offer(new int[]{e.getKey(), e.getValue()});            if (heap.size() > k) heap.poll();        }        int[] ans = new int[k];        for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--) ans[i] = heap.poll()[0];        return ans;    }}
CostO(n log k) time · O(n) space
TrapThe heap must be a MIN-heap by count so the weakest is the one thrown away.
Variations
Bucket sort version · O(n)
A value can appear at most n times, so put values into buckets by count and read from the top.
public int[] topKFrequent(int[] nums, int k) {    Map<Integer, Integer> cnt = new HashMap<>();    for (int x : nums) cnt.merge(x, 1, Integer::sum);    List<List<Integer>> bucket = new ArrayList<>();          // bucket.get(f) = values seen f times    for (int i = 0; i <= nums.length; i++) bucket.add(new ArrayList<>());    for (Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e : cnt.entrySet()) bucket.get(e.getValue()).add(e.getKey());    int[] ans = new int[k];    int idx = 0;    for (int f = nums.length; f >= 1 && idx < k; f--)        for (int v : bucket.get(f)) if (idx < k) ans[idx++] = v;    return ans;}
LC 215 · Kth Largest Element in an Array
The same "heap of size k" trick: a min-heap of the k largest; its top is the answer.
public int findKthLargest(int[] nums, int k) {    PriorityQueue<Integer> heap = new PriorityQueue<>();    for (int x : nums) {        heap.offer(x);        if (heap.size() > k) heap.poll();    }    return heap.peek();}
  • LC 692 Top K Frequent Words — Comparator (a, b) -> ca != cb ? ca - cb : b.compareTo(a) keeps alphabetical order on ties.
LC 729My Calendar IMediumDay 1 · #5
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3TreeMap neighbours
Spot itAccept a booking only if it overlaps nothing booked so far.
“Look at the neighbour on the left and on the right; nobody else can touch you.”
class MyCalendar {    private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> cal = new TreeMap<>();   // start -> end​    public MyCalendar() {}​    public boolean book(int startTime, int endTime) {        Integer prev = cal.floorKey(startTime);                   // starts at or before me        Integer next = cal.ceilingKey(startTime);                 // starts at or after me        if (prev != null && cal.get(prev) > startTime) return false;        if (next != null && next < endTime) return false;        cal.put(startTime, endTime);        return true;    }}
CostO(log n) per booking
TrapIntervals are half-open [start, end): end == next start is allowed, so compare with > and <, not >=.
Variations
LC 731 · My Calendar II (no triple booking)
Sweep line on a TreeMap of +1 / −1. Add the booking, walk the running count, undo if it ever reaches 3. (My Calendar III is Day 21.)
class MyCalendarTwo {    private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> diff = new TreeMap<>();​    public MyCalendarTwo() {}​    public boolean book(int startTime, int endTime) {        diff.merge(startTime, 1, Integer::sum);        diff.merge(endTime, -1, Integer::sum);        int active = 0;        for (int v : diff.values()) {            active += v;            if (active >= 3) {                          // triple booking: undo and refuse                diff.merge(startTime, -1, Integer::sum);                diff.merge(endTime, 1, Integer::sum);                return false;            }        }        return true;    }}
LC 206Reverse Linked ListEasyDay 1 · #6
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Linked list · three pointers
Spot itReverse a singly linked list in place.
“Save, flip, step, step.”
class Solution {    public ListNode reverseList(ListNode head) {        ListNode prev = null, cur = head;        while (cur != null) {            ListNode next = cur.next;     // save            cur.next = prev;              // flip            prev = cur;                   // step prev            cur = next;                   // step cur        }        return prev;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapReturn prev, not head: at the end cur is null and prev is the new head.
Variations
Recursive reverse
Same result, O(n) stack. Good to know; the loop is safer for long lists.
public ListNode reverseList(ListNode head) {    if (head == null || head.next == null) return head;    ListNode newHead = reverseList(head.next);    head.next.next = head;            // the node after head points back to head    head.next = null;    return newHead;}
LC 92 · Reverse Linked List II (positions left..right)
Dummy node, walk to the node before left, then move each next node to the front of the section.
public ListNode reverseBetween(ListNode head, int left, int right) {    ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0, head), before = dummy;    for (int i = 1; i < left; i++) before = before.next;    ListNode cur = before.next;    for (int i = 0; i < right - left; i++) {        ListNode move = cur.next;     // take the node after cur ...        cur.next = move.next;        move.next = before.next;      // ... and put it right after before        before.next = move;    }    return dummy.next;}
LC 141Linked List CycleEasyDay 1 · #7
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Fast and slow pointers
Spot itDoes the list loop back on itself? O(1) memory.
“The hare laps the tortoise only on a track.”
class Solution {    public boolean hasCycle(ListNode head) {        ListNode slow = head, fast = head;        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) {            slow = slow.next;            fast = fast.next.next;            if (slow == fast) return true;        }        return false;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapLoop condition is fast != null && fast.next != null, in that order.
Variations
LC 142 · Linked List Cycle II (where does the cycle start?)
After they meet, restart one pointer at head; move both one step; they meet at the cycle start.
public ListNode detectCycle(ListNode head) {    ListNode slow = head, fast = head;    while (fast != null && fast.next != null) {        slow = slow.next;        fast = fast.next.next;        if (slow == fast) {            ListNode p = head;            while (p != slow) { p = p.next; slow = slow.next; }            return p;        }    }    return null;}
  • LC 876 Middle of the Linked List — Same loop without the meet check; return slow (the second middle for even length).
LC 49Group AnagramsMediumDay 1 · #8
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3HashMap of lists · canonical key
Spot itGroup words that are anagrams of each other.
“Same sorted letters, same bucket.”
class Solution {    public List<List<String>> groupAnagrams(String[] strs) {        Map<String, List<String>> groups = new HashMap<>();        for (String s : strs) {            char[] c = s.toCharArray();            Arrays.sort(c);            groups.computeIfAbsent(new String(c), k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(s);        }        return new ArrayList<>(groups.values());    }}
CostO(n · L log L) time · O(n · L) space
Trapnew String(chars) for the key; chars.toString() gives an address, not the letters.
Variations
  • Count key, O(L) per word — Key = Arrays.toString(int[26] counts) instead of sorting.
Day 2

Prefix sums, difference arrays, hashing

Count subarrays by remembering earlier prefix values in a HashMap.

plan date Sun 8 Nov
learn these cards Wed 25 Nov
Pattern corePrefix sums: one array, four questions
P[i] = sum of the first i numbers, so sum(l..r) = P[r+1] − P[l]. Counting asks the map "how many earlier prefixes"; longest asks "where was the FIRST one".
static long[] prefix(int[] a) {                      // P[0] = 0, P[i+1] = P[i] + a[i]    long[] P = new long[a.length + 1];    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) P[i + 1] = P[i] + a[i];    return P;}​static int countSumK(int[] a, int k) {               // how many subarrays sum to k    Map<Integer, Integer> seen = new HashMap<>(Map.of(0, 1));    int p = 0, count = 0;    for (int x : a) {        p += x;        count += seen.getOrDefault(p - k, 0);        seen.merge(p, 1, Integer::sum);    }    return count;}​static int longestSumK(int[] a, int k) {             // longest subarray that sums to k    Map<Integer, Integer> first = new HashMap<>(Map.of(0, -1));    int p = 0, best = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {        p += a[i];        Integer j = first.get(p - k);        if (j != null) best = Math.max(best, i - j);        first.putIfAbsent(p, i);                     // keep the earliest index    }    return best;}​static int[] rangeAdds(int n, int[][] ups) {         // each {l, r, v}: add v to a[l..r]    int[] d = new int[n + 1];    for (int[] u : ups) { d[u[0]] += u[2]; d[u[1] + 1] -= u[2]; }    int[] a = new int[n];    for (int i = 0, run = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = run += d[i];    return a;}
LC 560Subarray Sum Equals KMediumDay 2 · #9
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Prefix sum + HashMap
Spot itCount subarrays with sum exactly k, and numbers can be negative.
“Seed zero, look back k, then count yourself.”
class Solution {    public int subarraySum(int[] nums, int k) {        Map<Integer, Integer> seen = new HashMap<>();   // prefix value -> how many times seen        seen.put(0, 1);                                  // the empty prefix        int prefix = 0, count = 0;        for (int x : nums) {            prefix += x;            count += seen.getOrDefault(prefix - k, 0);   // earlier p with prefix - p == k            seen.merge(prefix, 1, Integer::sum);         // count yourself AFTER looking        }        return count;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapA sliding window does NOT work with negative numbers. Forgetting seen.put(0, 1) misses subarrays that start at index 0.
Variations
Longest subarray with sum k (LC 325, premium)
Store the FIRST index of each prefix instead of a count, and seed {0: -1}.
public int maxSubArrayLen(int[] nums, int k) {    Map<Long, Integer> first = new HashMap<>();    first.put(0L, -1);    long prefix = 0;    int best = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {        prefix += nums[i];        Integer j = first.get(prefix - k);        if (j != null) best = Math.max(best, i - j);        first.putIfAbsent(prefix, i);                // never overwrite: earliest gives longest    }    return best;}

LC 974Subarray Sums Divisible by KMediumDay 2 · #10
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Prefix remainders
Spot itCount subarrays whose sum is divisible by k.
“Same remainder twice means the part between is divisible.”
class Solution {    public int subarraysDivByK(int[] nums, int k) {        int[] seen = new int[k];                         // seen[r] = prefixes with remainder r        seen[0] = 1;        int prefix = 0, count = 0;        for (int x : nums) {            prefix = Math.floorMod(prefix + x, k);       // never negative            count += seen[prefix];            seen[prefix]++;        }        return count;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(k) space
TrapIn Java -7 % 5 is -2. Use Math.floorMod so remainders are 0..k−1.
Variations
LC 523 · Continuous Subarray Sum (length ≥ 2, sum a multiple of k)
Remainder → FIRST index, seeded {0: -1}; succeed when the same remainder is at least 2 positions back.
public boolean checkSubarraySum(int[] nums, int k) {    Map<Integer, Integer> first = new HashMap<>();    first.put(0, -1);    int r = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {        r = (r + nums[i]) % k;                       // nums are non-negative here        Integer j = first.get(r);        if (j == null) first.put(r, i);        else if (i - j >= 2) return true;    }    return false;}
LC 1524Number of Sub-arrays With Odd SumMediumDay 2 · #11

Spot itCount subarrays with an odd sum (answer mod 10⁹+7).
“Odd minus even is odd: count the opposite parity.”
class Solution {    public int numOfSubarrays(int[] arr) {        final int MOD = 1_000_000_007;        long odd = 0, even = 1, count = 0;               // the empty prefix is even        int parity = 0;        for (int x : arr) {            parity = (parity + x) & 1;                   // only the parity of the prefix matters            if (parity == 1) { count += even; odd++; }   // odd now − even before = odd            else { count += odd; even++; }               // even now − odd before = odd        }        return (int) (count % MOD);    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapThe empty prefix (sum 0) is even, so start with even = 1.
Variations

public int longestWPI(int[] hours) {    Map<Integer, Integer> first = new HashMap<>();    int bal = 0, best = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < hours.length; i++) {        bal += hours[i] > 8 ? 1 : -1;        if (bal > 0) best = i + 1;                   // the whole prefix is good        else {            Integer j = first.get(bal - 1);          // first time we were one lower            if (j != null) best = Math.max(best, i - j);        }        first.putIfAbsent(bal, i);    }    return best;}

class Solution {    public int[] corpFlightBookings(int[][] bookings, int n) {        int[] d = new int[n + 1];        for (int[] b : bookings) {            d[b[0] - 1] += b[2];                         // start adding at first            d[b[1]] -= b[2];                             // stop after last        }        int[] ans = new int[n];        int run = 0;        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {            run += d[i];                                 // running sum = the real value            ans[i] = run;        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n + bookings) time · O(n) space

public boolean carPooling(int[][] trips, int capacity) {    int[] d = new int[1001];    for (int[] t : trips) { d[t[1]] += t[0]; d[t[2]] -= t[0]; }    int run = 0;    for (int x : d) if ((run += x) > capacity) return false;    return true;}

class NumMatrix {    private final int[][] P;   // P[i][j] = sum of rows 0..i-1, cols 0..j-1​    public NumMatrix(int[][] matrix) {        int m = matrix.length, n = matrix[0].length;        P = new int[m + 1][n + 1];        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++)            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)                P[i + 1][j + 1] = P[i][j + 1] + P[i + 1][j] - P[i][j] + matrix[i][j];    }​    public int sumRegion(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2) {        return P[row2 + 1][col2 + 1] - P[row1][col2 + 1] - P[row2 + 1][col1] + P[row1][col1];    }}
CostO(mn) build · O(1) per query

The same table; clamp each block's corners to the grid before the query.
public int[][] matrixBlockSum(int[][] mat, int k) {    int m = mat.length, n = mat[0].length;    int[][] P = new int[m + 1][n + 1];    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++)        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)            P[i + 1][j + 1] = P[i][j + 1] + P[i + 1][j] - P[i][j] + mat[i][j];    int[][] ans = new int[m][n];    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++)        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {            int r1 = Math.max(0, i - k), c1 = Math.max(0, j - k);            int r2 = Math.min(m - 1, i + k), c2 = Math.min(n - 1, j + k);            ans[i][j] = P[r2 + 1][c2 + 1] - P[r1][c2 + 1] - P[r2 + 1][c1] + P[r1][c1];        }    return ans;}

Day 3

Two pointers and sliding window

Grow the window on the right; shrink it on the left while it is invalid.

plan date Mon 9 Nov
learn these cards Thu 26 Nov
Pattern coreVariable sliding window: grow right, shrink left while broken
Works when the rule is monotone: if a window breaks the rule, every bigger window around it breaks it too (all numbers ≥ 0, "at most k" counts). Longest: update after shrinking. Shortest: update inside the shrink loop.
static int longestAtMostKDistinct(int[] a, int k) {    Map<Integer, Integer> cnt = new HashMap<>();    int best = 0;    for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {        cnt.merge(a[r], 1, Integer::sum);              // 1. add a[r]        while (cnt.size() > k) {                       // 2. broken? shrink from the left            if (cnt.merge(a[l], -1, Integer::sum) == 0) cnt.remove(a[l]);            l++;        }        best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);              // 3. valid window [l..r]    }    return best;}​static int shortestSumAtLeast(int[] a, int target) {  // LC 209, all a[i] > 0    int best = Integer.MAX_VALUE, sum = 0;    for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {        sum += a[r];        while (sum >= target) {                        // valid: record, then try smaller            best = Math.min(best, r - l + 1);            sum -= a[l++];        }    }    return best == Integer.MAX_VALUE ? 0 : best;}
LC 3Longest Substring Without Repeating CharactersMediumDay 3 · #15
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sliding window · counts
Spot itLongest substring with no repeated character.
“Grow right; while the new char is doubled, shrink left.”
class Solution {    public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) {        int[] cnt = new int[128];        int best = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < s.length(); r++) {            char c = s.charAt(r);            cnt[c]++;                                       // grow right            while (cnt[c] > 1) cnt[s.charAt(l++)]--;        // shrink while broken            best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);               // valid here        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(128) space
TrapUpdate the answer AFTER the shrink loop, when the window is valid again.
Variations
Jump version: remember the last index of each character
Instead of shrinking one by one, jump l past the previous copy of c. Math.max stops l from moving backwards.
public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) {    int[] last = new int[128];                          // last[c] = 1 + last index of c, 0 = never    int best = 0;    for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < s.length(); r++) {        char c = s.charAt(r);        l = Math.max(l, last[c]);        last[c] = r + 1;        best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);    }    return best;}

class Solution {    public int longestOnes(int[] nums, int k) {        int best = 0, zeros = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < nums.length; r++) {            if (nums[r] == 0) zeros++;            while (zeros > k) if (nums[l++] == 0) zeros--;            best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);        }        return best;    }}

class Solution {    public int characterReplacement(String s, int k) {        int[] cnt = new int[26];        int best = 0, maxCount = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < s.length(); r++) {            maxCount = Math.max(maxCount, ++cnt[s.charAt(r) - 'A']);            while (r - l + 1 - maxCount > k) cnt[s.charAt(l++) - 'A']--;   // too many to replace            best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);        }        return best;    }}

LC 153SumMediumDay 3 · #18
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sort + two pointers
Spot itAll unique triples that sum to 0.
“Sort, fix one, squeeze the other two, skip the twins.”
class Solution {    public List<List<Integer>> threeSum(int[] nums) {        Arrays.sort(nums);        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {            if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;              // skip twin for i            if (nums[i] > 0) break;                                     // smallest is positive: done            int l = i + 1, r = nums.length - 1;            while (l < r) {                int s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r];                if (s < 0) l++;                                         // too small: move l right                else if (s > 0) r--;                                    // too big: move r left                else {                    res.add(Arrays.asList(nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]));                    while (l < r && nums[l] == nums[l + 1]) l++;        // skip twins for l and r                    while (l < r && nums[r] == nums[r - 1]) r--;                    l++; r--;                }            }        }        return res;    }}
CostO(n²) time · O(1) extra space
TrapSkip duplicates for i (compare with i − 1) and for l and r after each hit, or you print the same triple twice.
Variations
LC 16 · 3Sum Closest
The same squeeze; keep the sum with the smallest |s − target|.
public int threeSumClosest(int[] nums, int target) {    Arrays.sort(nums);    int best = nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2];    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {        int l = i + 1, r = nums.length - 1;        while (l < r) {            int s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r];            if (Math.abs(s - target) < Math.abs(best - target)) best = s;            if (s < target) l++; else if (s > target) r--; else return s;        }    }    return best;}
LC 18 · 4Sum
One more outer loop with its own twin skip. The sum needs long: four values of 10⁹ overflow an int.
public List<List<Integer>> fourSum(int[] nums, int target) {    Arrays.sort(nums);    List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();    int n = nums.length;    for (int a = 0; a < n - 3; a++) {        if (a > 0 && nums[a] == nums[a - 1]) continue;        for (int b = a + 1; b < n - 2; b++) {            if (b > a + 1 && nums[b] == nums[b - 1]) continue;            int l = b + 1, r = n - 1;            while (l < r) {                long s = (long) nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[l] + nums[r];                if (s < target) l++;                else if (s > target) r--;                else {                    res.add(Arrays.asList(nums[a], nums[b], nums[l], nums[r]));                    while (l < r && nums[l] == nums[l + 1]) l++;                    while (l < r && nums[r] == nums[r - 1]) r--;                    l++; r--;                }            }        }    }    return res;}

“Exactly is hard, at most is a window: subtract two windows.”
class Solution {    public int subarraysWithKDistinct(int[] nums, int k) {        return atMost(nums, k) - atMost(nums, k - 1);    }​    private int atMost(int[] a, int k) {                        // subarrays with <= k distinct        int[] cnt = new int[a.length + 1];                      // values are 1..n        int distinct = 0, total = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {            if (cnt[a[r]]++ == 0) distinct++;            while (distinct > k) if (--cnt[a[l++]] == 0) distinct--;            total += r - l + 1;                                 // all subarrays ending at r        }        return total;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapIn atMost, add r − l + 1 (every subarray ending at r), not 1.
Variations
LC 1248 · Count Number of Nice Subarrays (exactly k odd numbers)
The same subtraction; the window counts odd numbers instead of distinct values. (LC 930 is the same with sums of 0/1.)
public int numberOfSubarrays(int[] nums, int k) {    return atMost(nums, k) - atMost(nums, k - 1);}​private int atMost(int[] a, int k) {    int odd = 0, total = 0;    for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {        odd += a[r] & 1;        while (odd > k) odd -= a[l++] & 1;        total += r - l + 1;    }    return total;}
LC 239Sliding Window MaximumHardDay 3 · #20
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Monotonic deque
Spot itThe maximum of every window of size k.
“Kick out the old from the front, kick out the small from the back; the front is the max.”
class Solution {    public int[] maxSlidingWindow(int[] nums, int k) {        int n = nums.length;        int[] ans = new int[n - k + 1];        Deque<Integer> dq = new ArrayDeque<>();                 // indices; their values decrease front -> back        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {            while (!dq.isEmpty() && dq.peekFirst() <= i - k) dq.pollFirst();          // left the window            while (!dq.isEmpty() && nums[dq.peekLast()] <= nums[i]) dq.pollLast();    // smaller: never the max again            dq.offerLast(i);            if (i >= k - 1) ans[i - k + 1] = nums[dq.peekFirst()];                    // front = max        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(k) space
TrapStore INDICES in the deque, so you can tell when the front has left the window.
Variations
LC 1438 · Longest Subarray with |max − min| ≤ limit
A variable window plus TWO deques (one for max, one for min). Shrink while max − min > limit.
public int longestSubarray(int[] nums, int limit) {    Deque<Integer> mx = new ArrayDeque<>(), mn = new ArrayDeque<>();   // values    int best = 0;    for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < nums.length; r++) {        while (!mx.isEmpty() && mx.peekLast() < nums[r]) mx.pollLast();        while (!mn.isEmpty() && mn.peekLast() > nums[r]) mn.pollLast();        mx.offerLast(nums[r]);        mn.offerLast(nums[r]);        while (mx.peekFirst() - mn.peekFirst() > limit) {            if (mx.peekFirst() == nums[l]) mx.pollFirst();   // nums[l] leaves: drop it if it is a front            if (mn.peekFirst() == nums[l]) mn.pollFirst();            l++;        }        best = Math.max(best, r - l + 1);    }    return best;}
LC 862 · Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K (negatives allowed)
Negatives break the plain window. Use prefix sums and a deque of indices with increasing prefix values.
public int shortestSubarray(int[] nums, int k) {    int n = nums.length;    long[] P = new long[n + 1];    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) P[i + 1] = P[i] + nums[i];    Deque<Integer> dq = new ArrayDeque<>();    int best = n + 1;    for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {        while (!dq.isEmpty() && P[i] - P[dq.peekFirst()] >= k) best = Math.min(best, i - dq.pollFirst());        while (!dq.isEmpty() && P[dq.peekLast()] >= P[i]) dq.pollLast();   // a later, lower start is better        dq.offerLast(i);    }    return best <= n ? best : -1;}
  • Window minimum — Flip the second comparison to nums[dq.peekLast()] >= nums[i].
LC 76Minimum Window SubstringHardDay 3 · #21
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sliding window · need vs have

class Solution {    public String minWindow(String s, String t) {        int[] need = new int[128];        for (char c : t.toCharArray()) need[c]++;        int missing = t.length(), bestL = 0, bestLen = Integer.MAX_VALUE;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < s.length(); r++) {            if (need[s.charAt(r)]-- > 0) missing--;             // we still needed this char            while (missing == 0) {                              // valid: record, then shrink                if (r - l + 1 < bestLen) { bestLen = r - l + 1; bestL = l; }                if (++need[s.charAt(l++)] > 0) missing++;       // dropped a char we need            }        }        return bestLen == Integer.MAX_VALUE ? "" : s.substring(bestL, bestL + bestLen);    }}
CostO(|s| + |t|) time · O(128) space
TrapRecord the answer INSIDE the shrink loop (before removing s[l]), because that is when the window is valid.

public boolean checkInclusion(String s1, String s2) {    int[] need = new int[26];    for (char c : s1.toCharArray()) need[c - 'a']++;    int missing = s1.length(), m = s1.length();    for (int r = 0; r < s2.length(); r++) {        if (need[s2.charAt(r) - 'a']-- > 0) missing--;        if (r >= m && ++need[s2.charAt(r - m) - 'a'] > 0) missing++;   // char leaving the window        if (missing == 0) return true;    }    return false;}
Day 4

Sorting and greedy: intervals

Sort by the right key, then make one decision per element. Check the greedy by swapping two choices.

plan date Tue 10 Nov
learn these cards Thu 26 Nov
Pattern coreIntervals: which end do you sort by?
Merge or insert → sort by START. Keep the most / fewest arrows / remove the fewest → sort by END and keep greedily. How many overlap at once → sort starts and ends separately (or +1/−1 events).
static int maxOverlap(int[][] iv) {                // closed intervals [s, e]    List<int[]> ev = new ArrayList<>();    for (int[] x : iv) { ev.add(new int[]{x[0], +1}); ev.add(new int[]{x[1] + 1, -1}); }    ev.sort((a, b) -> a[0] != b[0] ? Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]) : Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // -1 before +1 at a tie    int cur = 0, best = 0;    for (int[] e : ev) best = Math.max(best, cur += e[1]);    return best;}
LC 56Merge IntervalsMediumDay 4 · #22
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sort by start · merge
Spot itMerge all overlapping intervals.
“Sort by start; overlap stretches the last one, a gap starts a new one.”
class Solution {    public int[][] merge(int[][] intervals) {        Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));        List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();        for (int[] iv : intervals) {            int[] last = out.isEmpty() ? null : out.get(out.size() - 1);            if (last != null && iv[0] <= last[1]) last[1] = Math.max(last[1], iv[1]);  // overlap: stretch            else out.add(iv);                                                          // gap: new one        }        return out.toArray(new int[0][]);    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapExtend with Math.max(last[1], iv[1]): an interval can sit completely inside the last one.
Variations
LC 57 · Insert Interval (input already sorted, no sort needed)
Three phases: copy the ones fully left, absorb the overlapping ones, copy the rest.
public int[][] insert(int[][] intervals, int[] newInterval) {    List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();    int i = 0, n = intervals.length, s = newInterval[0], e = newInterval[1];    while (i < n && intervals[i][1] < s) out.add(intervals[i++]);      // ends before us    while (i < n && intervals[i][0] <= e) {                           // overlaps us: absorb        s = Math.min(s, intervals[i][0]);        e = Math.max(e, intervals[i][1]);        i++;    }    out.add(new int[]{s, e});    while (i < n) out.add(intervals[i++]);    return out.toArray(new int[0][]);}
LC 986 · Interval List Intersections
Two sorted lists, two pointers. The overlap is [max(starts), min(ends)]; advance the one that ends first.
public int[][] intervalIntersection(int[][] firstList, int[][] secondList) {    List<int[]> out = new ArrayList<>();    int i = 0, j = 0;    while (i < firstList.length && j < secondList.length) {        int lo = Math.max(firstList[i][0], secondList[j][0]);        int hi = Math.min(firstList[i][1], secondList[j][1]);        if (lo <= hi) out.add(new int[]{lo, hi});        if (firstList[i][1] < secondList[j][1]) i++; else j++;    }    return out.toArray(new int[0][]);}
LC 435Non-overlapping IntervalsMediumDay 4 · #23
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sort by end · keep greedily
Spot itRemove the fewest intervals so the rest do not overlap.
“Finish earliest, keep the most; removed = n − kept.”
class Solution {    public int eraseOverlapIntervals(int[][] intervals) {        Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // by END        int kept = 0;        long end = Long.MIN_VALUE;        for (int[] iv : intervals) {            if (iv[0] >= end) { kept++; end = iv[1]; }                 // fits after the last kept one        }        return intervals.length - kept;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(1) space
TrapSorting by START fails: one long early interval would block many short ones.
Variations
  • LC 646 Maximum Length of Pair Chain — Same loop, but chains need p[0] > end (strict); return kept.

Spot itFewest groups so that no two intervals in a group overlap (closed intervals).
“Sort starts and ends; a start after the earliest end reuses a group, otherwise open one.”
class Solution {    public int minGroups(int[][] intervals) {        int n = intervals.length;        int[] starts = new int[n], ends = new int[n];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { starts[i] = intervals[i][0]; ends[i] = intervals[i][1]; }        Arrays.sort(starts);        Arrays.sort(ends);        int groups = 0, j = 0;        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {            if (starts[i] > ends[j]) j++;                      // a group finished: reuse it            else groups++;                                     // all busy: open a new group        }        return groups;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapIntervals are inclusive, so reuse needs start > end (strictly). For half-open meetings (LC 253) use >=.
Variations
Heap version (also gives which group to reuse)
Sort by start; a min-heap holds the end of each open group. Its size at the end is the answer.
public int minGroups(int[][] intervals) {    Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));    PriorityQueue<Integer> ends = new PriorityQueue<>();    for (int[] iv : intervals) {        if (!ends.isEmpty() && ends.peek() < iv[0]) ends.poll();   // the group that ends first is free        ends.offer(iv[1]);    }    return ends.size();}
LC 179Largest NumberMediumDay 4 · #25
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Custom comparator
Spot itArrange numbers to form the largest number.
“Put a before b when a+b beats b+a.”
class Solution {    public String largestNumber(int[] nums) {        String[] s = new String[nums.length];        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) s[i] = String.valueOf(nums[i]);        Arrays.sort(s, (a, b) -> (b + a).compareTo(a + b));    // a first if a+b > b+a        if (s[0].equals("0")) return "0";        return String.join("", s);    }}
CostO(n log n · L) time · O(n · L) space
TrapAll zeros give "000"; return "0".
Variations
  • Smallest number — Use (a + b).compareTo(b + a) and strip leading zeros.
LC 1798Maximum Number of Consecutive Values You Can MakeMediumDay 4 · #26
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Greedy reach
Spot itHow many consecutive values 0, 1, 2 ... can the coins make?
“Sort; if the next coin fits inside reach + 1, reach grows by it; otherwise there is a hole.”
class Solution {    public int getMaximumConsecutive(int[] coins) {        Arrays.sort(coins);        int reach = 0;                               // every value 0..reach can be made        for (int c : coins) {            if (c > reach + 1) break;                // reach + 1 can never be made            reach += c;        }        return reach + 1;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(1) space
TrapThe answer counts 0 too, so return reach + 1.
Variations
LC 330 · Patching Array
The same reach; when the next number does not fit, the best patch is reach + 1, which doubles the reach.
public int minPatches(int[] nums, int n) {    long reach = 0;                              // can make 1..reach    int i = 0, patches = 0;    while (reach < n) {        if (i < nums.length && nums[i] <= reach + 1) reach += nums[i++];        else { reach += reach + 1; patches++; }    }    return patches;}
LC 452Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst BalloonsMediumDay 4 · #27
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Sort by end · arrows
Spot itFewest arrows to burst all balloons (touching counts).
“Shoot at the end of the first balloon; everything starting before it is gone.”
class Solution {    public int findMinArrowShots(int[][] points) {        Arrays.sort(points, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // by end, no subtraction        int arrows = 0;        long arrowAt = Long.MIN_VALUE;        for (int[] p : points) {            if (p[0] > arrowAt) { arrows++; arrowAt = p[1]; }          // not hit: new arrow at its end        }        return arrows;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(1) space
TrapValues reach ±2³¹: compare with Integer.compare, never a[1] − b[1].
LC 135CandyHardDay 4 · #28
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Two passes
Spot itEach child with a higher rating than a neighbour gets more candy; minimise the total.
“Left pass fixes left neighbours, right pass fixes right neighbours, keep the max.”
class Solution {    public int candy(int[] ratings) {        int n = ratings.length;        int[] c = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(c, 1);        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++)            if (ratings[i] > ratings[i - 1]) c[i] = c[i - 1] + 1;        for (int i = n - 2; i >= 0; i--)            if (ratings[i] > ratings[i + 1]) c[i] = Math.max(c[i], c[i + 1] + 1);        int sum = 0;        for (int x : c) sum += x;        return sum;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapIn the right pass use Math.max, or you break what the left pass fixed.
Variations
  • Same left/right idea — LC 42 Trapping Rain Water and LC 238 Product Except Self (Bonus A).
Day 5

Greedy with heaps

Unlock options in sorted order, keep the unlocked ones in a heap, undo your worst choice when a limit breaks.

plan date Wed 11 Nov
learn these cards Fri 27 Nov
Pattern coreGreedy + heap: unlock, then take the best
Two shapes. (1) Sort by what unlocks an option, push options as they unlock, pop the best (IPO, refuelling). (2) Take everything, keep the choices in a heap, and undo the worst one when you go over a limit (ladders, courses, potions).
static long unlockThenTake(int[][] items, long start, int picks) {   // items {cost, gain}    Arrays.sort(items, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));    PriorityQueue<Integer> gains = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());    long have = start;    for (int i = 0; picks-- > 0; ) {        while (i < items.length && items[i][0] <= have) gains.offer(items[i++][1]);        if (gains.isEmpty()) break;        have += gains.poll();    }    return have;}​static int keepWithUndo(int[] values, long limit) {   // most items with sum <= limit, in order    PriorityQueue<Integer> taken = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());    long sum = 0;    for (int v : values) {        taken.offer(v);        sum += v;        if (sum > limit) sum -= taken.poll();         // undo the most expensive choice so far    }    return taken.size();}
LC 502IPOHardDay 5 · #29
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Sort by capital + max-heap of profits
Spot itPick at most k projects; each needs capital you already have and adds its profit.
“Unlock everything you can afford, take the fattest, repeat k times.”
class Solution {    public int findMaximizedCapital(int k, int w, int[] profits, int[] capital) {        int n = profits.length;        int[][] proj = new int[n][];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) proj[i] = new int[]{capital[i], profits[i]};        Arrays.sort(proj, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));                  // by capital needed        PriorityQueue<Integer> best = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());   // affordable profits        int i = 0;        while (k-- > 0) {            while (i < n && proj[i][0] <= w) best.offer(proj[i++][1]);              // unlock            if (best.isEmpty()) break;            w += best.poll();                                                       // take the biggest        }        return w;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapIf nothing is affordable, stop early: the heap is empty.
Variations
  • Infosys RPG "defeat the most monsters" — Sort by power, walk while experience ≥ power (no heap: every bonus is ≥ 0).
LC 1642Furthest Building You Can ReachMediumDay 5 · #30
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Min-heap of ladder climbs
Spot itBricks pay any climb, ladders pay one climb each; how far can you go?
“Give every climb a ladder; when ladders run out, the smallest ladder climb pays bricks.”
class Solution {    public int furthestBuilding(int[] heights, int bricks, int ladders) {        PriorityQueue<Integer> climbs = new PriorityQueue<>();        // climbs currently using ladders        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < heights.length; i++) {            int d = heights[i + 1] - heights[i];            if (d <= 0) continue;            climbs.offer(d);                                          // ladder for now            if (climbs.size() > ladders) bricks -= climbs.poll();     // smallest one pays bricks            if (bricks < 0) return i;        }        return heights.length - 1;    }}
CostO(n log L) time · O(L) space
TrapReturn i (the building you are standing on) when bricks go negative, not i + 1.
LC 1526Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target ArrayHardDay 5 · #31
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Count the rises
Spot itFewest "add 1 to a subarray" operations to build target from zeros.
“Every rise starts new operations; a fall just ends some.”
class Solution {    public int minNumberOperations(int[] target) {        int ops = target[0];        for (int i = 1; i < target.length; i++)            ops += Math.max(0, target[i] - target[i - 1]);    // only rises cost        return ops;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapStart with target[0]: climbing from 0 to the first height counts too.
Variations
LC 3229 · Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal to Target (+1 and −1 on subarrays)
Work on d = target − nums. Inside a run of the same sign, only growth in size costs; a sign change starts fresh.
public long minimumOperations(int[] nums, int[] target) {    long ops = 0;    int prev = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {        int d = target[i] - nums[i];        if (d > 0 && prev > 0) ops += Math.max(0, d - prev);        else if (d < 0 && prev < 0) ops += Math.max(0, prev - d);        else ops += Math.abs(d);        prev = d;    }    return ops;}
  • Start from an array nums instead of zeros — Run it on d[i] = target[i] − nums[i] when all d[i] ≥ 0.
LC 1046Last Stone WeightEasyDay 5 · #32
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Max-heap simulation
Spot itSmash the two heaviest stones until at most one is left.
“Poll two, push the difference.”
class Solution {    public int lastStoneWeight(int[] stones) {        PriorityQueue<Integer> heap = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());        for (int s : stones) heap.offer(s);        while (heap.size() > 1) {            int y = heap.poll(), x = heap.poll();             // the two heaviest            if (y != x) heap.offer(y - x);        }        return heap.isEmpty() ? 0 : heap.peek();    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapPriorityQueue is a MIN-heap; pass Collections.reverseOrder().
Variations
LC 2558 · Take Gifts From the Richest Pile
The same max-heap loop: k times, replace the top with its floor square root.
public long pickGifts(int[] gifts, int k) {    PriorityQueue<Integer> heap = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());    for (int g : gifts) heap.offer(g);    while (k-- > 0) heap.offer((int) Math.sqrt(heap.poll()));    long sum = 0;    for (int g : heap) sum += g;    return sum;}

LC 871Minimum Number of Refueling StopsHardDay 5 · #33
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Refuel in hindsight
Spot itFewest refuelling stops to reach target; stations along a line.
“Drive as far as you can; when stuck, pretend you stopped at the biggest station you passed.”
class Solution {    public int minRefuelStops(int target, int startFuel, int[][] stations) {        PriorityQueue<Integer> passed = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());        long reach = startFuel;        int stops = 0, i = 0;        while (reach < target) {            while (i < stations.length && stations[i][0] <= reach) passed.offer(stations[i++][1]);            if (passed.isEmpty()) return -1;                                                    // stuck            reach += passed.poll();                                                             // biggest so far            stops++;        }        return stops;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
Trapreach can pass 2³¹ (fuel values up to 10⁹), so keep it in a long.
Variations
DP version: dp[t] = farthest reach with t stops
O(n²) and needs no heap. Loop t downwards so each station is used at most once (0/1 knapsack idea).
public int minRefuelStops(int target, int startFuel, int[][] stations) {    int n = stations.length;    long[] dp = new long[n + 1];    dp[0] = startFuel;    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)        for (int t = i; t >= 0; t--)            if (dp[t] >= stations[i][0]) dp[t + 1] = Math.max(dp[t + 1], dp[t] + stations[i][1]);    for (int t = 0; t <= n; t++) if (dp[t] >= target) return t;    return -1;}
LC 630Course Schedule IIIHardDay 5 · #34
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Sort by deadline + max-heap undo
Spot itMost courses you can finish, each with a duration and a last day.
“Take courses by deadline; when late, throw out the longest one taken.”
class Solution {    public int scheduleCourse(int[][] courses) {        Arrays.sort(courses, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));                 // by deadline        PriorityQueue<Integer> taken = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());   // durations        int time = 0;        for (int[] c : courses) {            taken.offer(c[0]);            time += c[0];            if (time > c[1]) time -= taken.poll();                                   // late: drop the longest        }        return taken.size();    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapDrop the LONGEST course so far (it may be the current one), not the last one.
Variations
LC 1353 · Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended
Walk the days; a min-heap holds end days of events that have started. Each day attend the one that ends first.
public int maxEvents(int[][] events) {    Arrays.sort(events, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));    PriorityQueue<Integer> ends = new PriorityQueue<>();    int i = 0, n = events.length, attended = 0;    for (int day = 1; i < n || !ends.isEmpty(); day++) {        if (ends.isEmpty() && i < n && events[i][0] > day) day = events[i][0];   // skip empty days        while (i < n && events[i][0] == day) ends.offer(events[i++][1]);        while (!ends.isEmpty() && ends.peek() < day) ends.poll();                // expired        if (!ends.isEmpty()) { ends.poll(); attended++; }    }    return attended;}

Day 6

Binary search, including on the answer

When "can the answer be x?" is monotone, binary search x and check it greedily.

plan date Thu 12 Nov
learn these cards Fri 27 Nov
Pattern coreBinary search: one loop shape for everything
Picture the answers as false false … true true. Find the first true with hi = mid / lo = mid + 1. For the last true (true … false), round mid UP and use lo = mid / hi = mid − 1, or the loop never ends.
static int lowerBound(int[] a, int x) {           // first i with a[i] >= x (a.length if none)    int lo = 0, hi = a.length;    while (lo < hi) {        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;        if (a[mid] < x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;    }    return lo;}​static int upperBound(int[] a, int x) {           // first i with a[i] > x    int lo = 0, hi = a.length;    while (lo < hi) {        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;        if (a[mid] <= x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;    }    return lo;}​static long firstTrue(long lo, long hi, LongPredicate ok) {   // smallest x in [lo, hi] with ok(x)    while (lo < hi) {        long mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;        if (ok.test(mid)) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;    }    return lo;}​static long lastTrue(long lo, long hi, LongPredicate ok) {    // largest x in [lo, hi] with ok(x)    while (lo < hi) {        long mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2;                       // round UP        if (ok.test(mid)) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;    }    return lo;}
LC 34Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted ArrayMediumDay 6 · #35
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Lower bound twice
Spot itFirst and last position of a value in a sorted array.
“First ≥ x, and first ≥ x + 1, minus one.”
class Solution {    public int[] searchRange(int[] nums, int target) {        int first = lowerBound(nums, target);        if (first == nums.length || nums[first] != target) return new int[]{-1, -1};        return new int[]{first, lowerBound(nums, target + 1) - 1};    }​    private int lowerBound(int[] a, int x) {           // first i with a[i] >= x        int lo = 0, hi = a.length;                     // hi = length, not length - 1        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;            if (a[mid] < x) lo = mid + 1;              // too small: answer is right of mid            else hi = mid;                             // mid may be the answer        }        return lo;    }}
CostO(log n) time · O(1) space
Traphi starts at a.length (the answer may be "past the end"), and the loop is lo < hi.
Variations
  • LC 35 Search Insert Position — It IS lowerBound(nums, target).
  • LC 278 First Bad Version — firstTrue(1, n, isBadVersion).
LC 875Koko Eating BananasMediumDay 6 · #36
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search on the answer · smallest that works
Spot itSmallest eating speed that finishes all piles within h hours.
“Guess a speed, count the hours; too slow, go up; fast enough, try lower.”
class Solution {    public int minEatingSpeed(int[] piles, int h) {        int lo = 1, hi = 1_000_000_000;                // the range of possible answers        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;            if (hours(piles, mid) <= h) hi = mid;      // fast enough: try slower            else lo = mid + 1;        }        return lo;    }​    private long hours(int[] piles, int speed) {        long total = 0;        for (int p : piles) total += (p - 1) / speed + 1;   // ceil(p / speed)        return total;    }}
CostO(n log max) time · O(1) space
Trap(p + speed − 1) / speed overflows int for p, speed near 10⁹. Use (p − 1) / speed + 1, and sum the hours in a long.
LC 1011Capacity To Ship Packages Within D DaysMediumDay 6 · #37
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search on the answer + greedy check
Spot itSmallest ship capacity to ship packages in order within D days.
“Capacity between the heaviest box and the total; fill each day greedily to check.”
class Solution {    public int shipWithinDays(int[] weights, int days) {        int lo = 0, hi = 0;        for (int w : weights) { lo = Math.max(lo, w); hi += w; }        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;            if (daysNeeded(weights, mid) <= days) hi = mid;            else lo = mid + 1;        }        return lo;    }​    private int daysNeeded(int[] weights, int cap) {        int d = 1, load = 0;        for (int w : weights) {            if (load + w > cap) { d++; load = 0; }      // full: start the next day            load += w;        }        return d;    }}
CostO(n log sum) time · O(1) space
TrapThe low end is the HEAVIEST package, or one box never fits.
Variations
  • Book allocation / painter's partition (GfG) — The same code; "pages" or "boards" instead of weights.
LC 410Split Array Largest SumHardDay 6 · #38
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search on the answer (same check as 1011)
Spot itSplit into k contiguous parts and minimise the largest part sum.
“It is the ship problem: days = k, capacity = largest sum.”
class Solution {    public int splitArray(int[] nums, int k) {        int lo = 0, hi = 0;        for (int x : nums) { lo = Math.max(lo, x); hi += x; }        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;            if (parts(nums, mid) <= k) hi = mid;            else lo = mid + 1;        }        return lo;    }​    private int parts(int[] a, int limit) {        int cnt = 1, sum = 0;        for (int x : a) {            if (sum + x > limit) { cnt++; sum = 0; }            sum += x;        }        return cnt;    }}
CostO(n log sum) time · O(1) space
TrapCount parts greedily and compare parts ≤ k; fewer parts is fine because you can always cut more.
Variations
  • DP version — dp[j][i] = best for the first i numbers in j parts (Day 21 shows the k-parts DP).
LC 1552Magnetic Force Between Two BallsMediumDay 6 · #39
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search on the answer · largest that works
Spot itPlace m balls in baskets to maximise the smallest gap.
“Guess a gap, place greedily from the left; it fits, go bigger.”
class Solution {    public int maxDistance(int[] position, int m) {        Arrays.sort(position);        int lo = 1, hi = position[position.length - 1] - position[0];        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2;                // round up            if (canPlace(position, m, mid)) lo = mid;            else hi = mid - 1;        }        return lo;    }​    private boolean canPlace(int[] pos, int m, int gap) {        int placed = 1, last = pos[0];        for (int i = 1; i < pos.length && placed < m; i++)            if (pos[i] - last >= gap) { placed++; last = pos[i]; }   // first spot far enough        return placed >= m;    }}
CostO(n log n + n log range) time · O(1) space
TrapSearching for the LARGEST, so mid = lo + (hi − lo + 1) / 2, or lo = mid loops forever.
Variations
  • Aggressive Cows (GfG/SPOJ), LC 2517 Maximum Tastiness of Candy Basket — The same code.
LC 2226Maximum Candies Allocated to K ChildrenMediumDay 6 · #40
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search on the answer · largest that works
Spot itLargest equal pile size x so at least k children get one pile of x candies.
“Children fed by x is the sum of pile / x; keep the largest x that feeds k.”
class Solution {    public int maximumCandies(int[] candies, long k) {        int lo = 0, hi = 0;        for (int c : candies) hi = Math.max(hi, c);        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2;                // round up: mid is never 0            long kids = 0;            for (int c : candies) kids += c / mid;            if (kids >= k) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;        }        return lo;    }}
CostO(n log max) time · O(1) space
TrapThe answer can be 0, so lo = 0; k is a long, so count children in a long.
LC 719Find K-th Smallest Pair DistanceHardDay 6 · #41
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Binary search the value + count with two pointers
Spot itThe k-th smallest distance among all pairs.
“Guess d, count pairs ≤ d with a sliding window; the first d with count ≥ k.”
class Solution {    public int smallestDistancePair(int[] nums, int k) {        Arrays.sort(nums);        int lo = 0, hi = nums[nums.length - 1] - nums[0];        while (lo < hi) {            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;            if (pairsAtMost(nums, mid) >= k) hi = mid;            else lo = mid + 1;        }        return lo;    }​    private long pairsAtMost(int[] a, int d) {        long cnt = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = 0; r < a.length; r++) {            while (a[r] - a[l] > d) l++;                    // window where every pair is <= d            cnt += r - l;                                   // pairs (l..r-1, r)        }        return cnt;    }}
CostO(n log n + n log W) time · O(1) space
TrapCount pairs in a long: n = 10⁴ gives 5·10⁷ pairs, fine, but the habit saves you on bigger n.
Variations
LC 378 · Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
Binary search the value; count cells ≤ mid with a staircase walk from the bottom-left corner.
public int kthSmallest(int[][] matrix, int k) {    int n = matrix.length, lo = matrix[0][0], hi = matrix[n - 1][n - 1];    while (lo < hi) {        int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, cnt = 0;        for (int r = n - 1, c = 0; r >= 0 && c < n; ) {            if (matrix[r][c] <= mid) { cnt += r + 1; c++; }   // whole column part counts            else r--;        }        if (cnt >= k) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;    }    return lo;}

Day 7

Monotonic stacks

Next or previous greater/smaller element for every index in O(n), and the contribution trick.

plan date Fri 13 Nov
learn these cards Sat 28 Nov
Pattern coreMonotonic stack: everyone waiting for a bigger (or smaller) neighbour
The stack holds indices still waiting for their answer. Pop while the top is beaten by the current element; the current element IS the answer for whatever you pop. Next greater: pop while a[top] < a[i]. Next smaller: pop while a[top] > a[i]. After popping, the new top is the PREVIOUS greater-or-equal (or smaller-or-equal) element.
static int[] nextGreater(int[] a) {               // index of the next strictly greater element, -1 if none    int n = a.length;    int[] nxt = new int[n];    Arrays.fill(nxt, -1);    Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {        while (!st.isEmpty() && a[st.peek()] < a[i]) nxt[st.pop()] = i;        st.push(i);    }    return nxt;}​static int[] previousSmaller(int[] a) {           // index of the previous strictly smaller element, -1 if none    int n = a.length;    int[] prev = new int[n];    Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {        while (!st.isEmpty() && a[st.peek()] >= a[i]) st.pop();        prev[i] = st.isEmpty() ? -1 : st.peek();        st.push(i);    }    return prev;}
LC 739Daily TemperaturesMediumDay 7 · #42
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Next greater element
Spot itFor each day, how many days until a warmer one?
“Days wait on the stack; a warmer day pops them and answers them.”
class Solution {    public int[] dailyTemperatures(int[] temperatures) {        int n = temperatures.length;        int[] ans = new int[n];        Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();                                   // days still waiting        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {            while (!st.isEmpty() && temperatures[st.peek()] < temperatures[i]) {                int j = st.pop();                ans[j] = i - j;                                                   // day i answers day j            }            st.push(i);        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapPush INDICES, not temperatures: the answer is a distance.
Variations
LC 901 · Online Stock Span
Previous greater element, online. Each stack entry carries the span it already absorbed.
class StockSpanner {    private final Deque<int[]> st = new ArrayDeque<>();   // {price, span}, prices decreasing​    public StockSpanner() {}​    public int next(int price) {        int span = 1;        while (!st.isEmpty() && st.peek()[0] <= price) span += st.pop()[1];        st.push(new int[]{price, span});        return span;    }}

LC 503Next Greater Element IIMediumDay 7 · #43

Spot itNext greater element when the array wraps around.
“Walk twice, push only on the first lap.”
class Solution {    public int[] nextGreaterElements(int[] nums) {        int n = nums.length;        int[] ans = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(ans, -1);        Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (int i = 0; i < 2 * n; i++) {                            // two laps            int x = nums[i % n];            while (!st.isEmpty() && nums[st.peek()] < x) ans[st.pop()] = x;            if (i < n) st.push(i);                                   // push on lap one only        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapPushing during the second lap gives wrong answers for duplicates; push only when i < n.
LC 84Largest Rectangle in HistogramHardDay 7 · #44
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Previous / next smaller bar
Spot itLargest rectangle in a histogram.
“When a bar is popped, the current bar is its right wall and the new top is its left wall.”
class Solution {    public int largestRectangleArea(int[] heights) {        int n = heights.length, best = 0;        Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();                      // increasing heights        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {            int h = i == n ? 0 : heights[i];                         // sentinel flushes the stack            while (!st.isEmpty() && heights[st.peek()] >= h) {                int height = heights[st.pop()];                      // shortest bar of its rectangle                int left = st.isEmpty() ? -1 : st.peek();            // previous smaller bar                best = Math.max(best, height * (i - left - 1));      // i = next smaller bar            }            st.push(i);        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapAdd a height-0 bar at the end (i == n) so every bar gets popped.
Variations
LC 85 · Maximal Rectangle (binary matrix)
Each row turns into a histogram of "1s stacked above". Reuse largestRectangleArea from the card above for every row.
public int maximalRectangle(char[][] matrix) {    int n = matrix[0].length, best = 0;    int[] h = new int[n];    for (char[] row : matrix) {        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) h[j] = row[j] == '1' ? h[j] + 1 : 0;        best = Math.max(best, largestRectangleArea(h));    }    return best;}
LC 907Sum of Subarray MinimumsMediumDay 7 · #45
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Contribution counting
Spot itSum of the minimum of every subarray (mod 10⁹+7).
“Each element is the minimum of (choices on the left) × (choices on the right) subarrays.”
class Solution {    public int sumSubarrayMins(int[] arr) {        final long MOD = 1_000_000_007L;        int n = arr.length;        int[] left = new int[n], right = new int[n];        Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {                                    // left: back to the previous <= element            while (!st.isEmpty() && arr[st.peek()] > arr[i]) st.pop();   // strict here            left[i] = st.isEmpty() ? i + 1 : i - st.peek();            st.push(i);        }        st.clear();        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {                               // right: up to the next < element            while (!st.isEmpty() && arr[st.peek()] >= arr[i]) st.pop();  // not strict here            right[i] = st.isEmpty() ? n - i : st.peek() - i;            st.push(i);        }        long sum = 0;        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)            sum = (sum + (long) arr[i] * left[i] % MOD * right[i]) % MOD;   // value × count        return (int) sum;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapWith equal values, use > on one side and >= on the other, so each subarray is counted exactly once.
Variations
  • Sum of subarray MAXIMUMS — Flip both comparisons (< and <=).

learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Greedy stack · smallest number
