LC 1091Shortest Path in Binary MatrixMediumDay 15 · #91
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalBFS · 8 directions
Spot itShortest clear path from top-left to bottom-right moving in 8 directions.
“BFS by layers; the path length counts cells, so the start is 1.”
class Solution {    public int shortestPathBinaryMatrix(int[][] grid) {        int n = grid.length;        if (grid[0][0] == 1 || grid[n - 1][n - 1] == 1) return -1;        Deque<int[]> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        q.offer(new int[]{0, 0});        grid[0][0] = 1;                                                     // visited        for (int dist = 1; !q.isEmpty(); dist++) {                          // counts cells            for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {                int[] c = q.poll();                if (c[0] == n - 1 && c[1] == n - 1) return dist;                for (int dr = -1; dr <= 1; dr++)                    for (int dc = -1; dc <= 1; dc++) {                      // 8 neighbours                        int r = c[0] + dr, col = c[1] + dc;                        if (r < 0 || col < 0 || r >= n || col >= n || grid[r][col] != 0) continue;                        grid[r][col] = 1;                        q.offer(new int[]{r, col});                    }            }        }        return -1;    }}
CostO(n²) time · O(n²) space
TrapIf the start or the end cell is blocked, return −1 immediately.
Variations
LC 1293 · Shortest Path with Obstacles Elimination (BFS over states)
When the rules carry a budget, the state is (row, col, budget left). Same BFS, a 3-D visited array.
public int shortestPath(int[][] grid, int k) {    int m = grid.length, n = grid[0].length;    boolean[][][] seen = new boolean[m][n][k + 1];    Deque<int[]> q = new ArrayDeque<>();    q.offer(new int[]{0, 0, k});    seen[0][0][k] = true;    int[] dr = {1, -1, 0, 0}, dc = {0, 0, 1, -1};    for (int steps = 0; !q.isEmpty(); steps++) {        for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {            int[] c = q.poll();            if (c[0] == m - 1 && c[1] == n - 1) return steps;            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {                int r = c[0] + dr[d], col = c[1] + dc[d];                if (r < 0 || col < 0 || r >= m || col >= n) continue;                int left = c[2] - grid[r][col];                   // a wall uses one removal                if (left < 0 || seen[r][col][left]) continue;                seen[r][col][left] = true;                q.offer(new int[]{r, col, left});            }        }    }    return -1;}
LC 785Is Graph Bipartite?MediumDay 15 · #92
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalBFS two-colouring
Spot itCan the nodes be split into two sides with every edge crossing?
“Colour the start 1, neighbours −1; a neighbour with my colour means an odd cycle.”
class Solution {    public boolean isBipartite(int[][] graph) {        int n = graph.length;        int[] color = new int[n];                                     // 0 = none, 1 / -1 = sides        for (int s = 0; s < n; s++) {            if (color[s] != 0) continue;            color[s] = 1;            Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();            q.offer(s);            while (!q.isEmpty()) {                int u = q.poll();                for (int v : graph[u]) {                    if (color[v] == color[u]) return false;                    if (color[v] == 0) { color[v] = -color[u]; q.offer(v); }                }            }        }        return true;    }}
CostO(V + E) time · O(V) space
TrapThe graph may be disconnected: start a BFS from every uncoloured node.
Variations
  • LC 886 Possible Bipartition — Build the graph from the dislike pairs (1-indexed), then this code.
LC 1368Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a GridHardDay 15 · #93
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4final0-1 BFS
Spot itEach cell has an arrow; changing an arrow costs 1. Cheapest way to reach the corner.
“Following the arrow costs 0 → push to the FRONT; changing it costs 1 → push to the BACK.”
class Solution {    public int minCost(int[][] grid) {        int m = grid.length, n = grid[0].length;        int[] dr = {0, 0, 1, -1}, dc = {1, -1, 0, 0};                // signs 1 right, 2 left, 3 down, 4 up        int[][] dist = new int[m][n];        for (int[] row : dist) Arrays.fill(row, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        dist[0][0] = 0;        Deque<int[]> dq = new ArrayDeque<>();        dq.offerFirst(new int[]{0, 0});        while (!dq.isEmpty()) {            int[] c = dq.pollFirst();            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {                int r = c[0] + dr[d], col = c[1] + dc[d];                if (r < 0 || col < 0 || r >= m || col >= n) continue;                int w = grid[c[0]][c[1]] == d + 1 ? 0 : 1;                 // free along the arrow                if (dist[c[0]][c[1]] + w < dist[r][col]) {                    dist[r][col] = dist[c[0]][c[1]] + w;                    if (w == 0) dq.offerFirst(new int[]{r, col});                    else dq.offerLast(new int[]{r, col});                }            }        }        return dist[m - 1][n - 1];    }}
CostO(m·n) time · O(m·n) space
TrapRelax with a dist array; a cell can be pushed more than once, and the check skips worse copies.
Variations
  • Dijkstra — Also correct, just a log factor slower.
LC 2050Parallel Courses IIIHardDay 15 · #94
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalTopological order + longest path DP
Spot itCourses take time[i] months, unlimited in parallel; earliest finish of everything.
“A course finishes at its own time plus the slowest prerequisite.”
class Solution {    public int minimumTime(int n, int[][] relations, int[] time) {        List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        int[] indeg = new int[n];        for (int[] r : relations) { g.get(r[0] - 1).add(r[1] - 1); indeg[r[1] - 1]++; }        int[] finish = new int[n];        Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (indeg[i] == 0) { q.offer(i); finish[i] = time[i]; }        int ans = 0;        while (!q.isEmpty()) {            int u = q.poll();            ans = Math.max(ans, finish[u]);            for (int v : g.get(u)) {                finish[v] = Math.max(finish[v], finish[u] + time[v]);       // wait for the slowest                if (--indeg[v] == 0) q.offer(v);            }        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(V + E) time · O(V + E) space
TrapInput is 1-indexed. Courses with no prerequisites finish at time[i].
Variations
LC 1857 · Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
The same Kahn order carrying cnt[v][26]: the most nodes of each colour on any path ending at v. A cycle means −1.
public int largestPathValue(String colors, int[][] edges) {    int n = colors.length();    List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());    int[] indeg = new int[n];    for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); indeg[e[1]]++; }    int[][] cnt = new int[n][26];    Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (indeg[i] == 0) q.offer(i);    int seen = 0, best = 0;    while (!q.isEmpty()) {        int u = q.poll();        seen++;        best = Math.max(best, ++cnt[u][colors.charAt(u) - 'a']);        for (int v : g.get(u)) {            for (int c = 0; c < 26; c++) cnt[v][c] = Math.max(cnt[v][c], cnt[u][c]);            if (--indeg[v] == 0) q.offer(v);        }    }    return seen == n ? best : -1;}
Day 17

Graphs II: Dijkstra, DSU, MST

Weighted shortest paths, expanded state graphs, union-find and Kruskal.

plan date Mon 23 Nov
learn these cards Wed 2 Dec
Pattern coreDijkstra and DSU
Dijkstra: pop the closest node; if the popped distance is bigger than dist[u], it is a stale copy, skip it. Only for non-negative weights. DSU: find with path halving, union by size; two nodes are connected iff their roots match.
static long[] dijkstra(List<List<int[]>> g, int src) {        // g.get(u) = {v, w}    long[] dist = new long[g.size()];    Arrays.fill(dist, Long.MAX_VALUE);    dist[src] = 0;    PriorityQueue<long[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(a[1], b[1]));    pq.offer(new long[]{src, 0});    while (!pq.isEmpty()) {        long[] cur = pq.poll();        int u = (int) cur[0];        if (cur[1] > dist[u]) continue;                        // stale        for (int[] e : g.get(u))            if (dist[u] + e[1] < dist[e[0]]) {                dist[e[0]] = dist[u] + e[1];                pq.offer(new long[]{e[0], dist[e[0]]});            }    }    return dist;}​static final class DSU {    final int[] parent, size;​    DSU(int n) {        parent = new int[n];        size = new int[n];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { parent[i] = i; size[i] = 1; }    }​    int find(int x) {        while (parent[x] != x) x = parent[x] = parent[parent[x]];   // path halving        return x;    }​    boolean union(int a, int b) {                              // false if already together        a = find(a);        b = find(b);        if (a == b) return false;        if (size[a] < size[b]) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }        parent[b] = a;        size[a] += size[b];        return true;    }}
LC 743Network Delay TimeMediumDay 17 · #95
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalDijkstra
Spot itTime for a signal from k to reach every node (directed, non-negative weights).
“Pop the closest, skip if stale, relax the neighbours; the answer is the farthest node.”
class Solution {    public int networkDelayTime(int[][] times, int n, int k) {        List<List<int[]>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] t : times) g.get(t[0]).add(new int[]{t[1], t[2]});        int[] dist = new int[n + 1];        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        dist[k] = 0;        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // {node, dist}        pq.offer(new int[]{k, 0});        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {            int[] cur = pq.poll();            int u = cur[0];            if (cur[1] > dist[u]) continue;                                  // stale            for (int[] e : g.get(u)) {                int v = e[0], nd = cur[1] + e[1];                if (nd < dist[v]) { dist[v] = nd; pq.offer(new int[]{v, nd}); }   // relax            }        }        int ans = 0;        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {            if (dist[i] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) return -1;            ans = Math.max(ans, dist[i]);        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(E log E) time · O(V + E) space
TrapNodes are 1..n: size the arrays n + 1 and ignore index 0 when taking the max.
Variations
LC 1334 · Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors (Floyd–Warshall)
All pairs, n ≤ 100: three loops with k OUTSIDE. Use a big value that is safe to add twice.
public int findTheCity(int n, int[][] edges, int distanceThreshold) {    int[][] d = new int[n][n];    for (int[] row : d) Arrays.fill(row, 1_000_000_000);    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) d[i][i] = 0;    for (int[] e : edges) {        d[e[0]][e[1]] = Math.min(d[e[0]][e[1]], e[2]);        d[e[1]][e[0]] = Math.min(d[e[1]][e[0]], e[2]);    }    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++)        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)                if (d[i][k] + d[k][j] < d[i][j]) d[i][j] = d[i][k] + d[k][j];    int best = -1, bestCount = Integer.MAX_VALUE;    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {        int cnt = 0;        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) if (d[i][j] <= distanceThreshold) cnt++;        if (cnt <= bestCount) { bestCount = cnt; best = i; }     // ties: larger index wins    }    return best;}

LC 1631Path With Minimum EffortMediumDay 17 · #96
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalDijkstra with a max-cost path
Spot itPath from top-left to bottom-right minimising the biggest height step.
“Dijkstra where a path costs its worst step: max(cur, step) instead of cur + step.”
class Solution {    public int minimumEffortPath(int[][] heights) {        int m = heights.length, n = heights[0].length;        int[][] effort = new int[m][n];        for (int[] row : effort) Arrays.fill(row, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        effort[0][0] = 0;        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[2], b[2]));   // {r, c, effort}        pq.offer(new int[]{0, 0, 0});        int[] dr = {1, -1, 0, 0}, dc = {0, 0, 1, -1};        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {            int[] cur = pq.poll();            int r = cur[0], c = cur[1];            if (cur[2] > effort[r][c]) continue;            if (r == m - 1 && c == n - 1) return cur[2];            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {                int nr = r + dr[d], nc = c + dc[d];                if (nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= m || nc >= n) continue;                int e = Math.max(cur[2], Math.abs(heights[nr][nc] - heights[r][c]));   // worst step so far                if (e < effort[nr][nc]) { effort[nr][nc] = e; pq.offer(new int[]{nr, nc, e}); }            }        }        return 0;    }}
CostO(mn log mn) time · O(mn) space
TrapYou may return as soon as the target is POPPED (not when it is pushed).
Variations
  • LC 778 Swim in Rising Water — Same code with cost max(cur, grid[nr][nc]).
LC 1584Min Cost to Connect All PointsMediumDay 17 · #97
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalMST · Prim O(n²)
Spot itConnect all points with Manhattan-distance edges at minimum total cost.
“Grow one tree: add the closest outside point, then let it lower everyone's distance.”
class Solution {    public int minCostConnectPoints(int[][] points) {        int n = points.length, total = 0;        int[] best = new int[n];                                    // cheapest edge from the tree to i        boolean[] inTree = new boolean[n];        Arrays.fill(best, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        best[0] = 0;        for (int it = 0; it < n; it++) {            int u = -1;            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)                if (!inTree[i] && (u == -1 || best[i] < best[u])) u = i;   // closest outside point            inTree[u] = true;            total += best[u];            for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) {                if (inTree[v]) continue;                int d = Math.abs(points[u][0] - points[v][0]) + Math.abs(points[u][1] - points[v][1]);                if (d < best[v]) best[v] = d;                       // u may be closer            }        }        return total;    }}
CostO(n²) time · O(n) space
TrapWith a complete graph, O(n²) Prim beats Kruskal's O(n² log n) sort.
Variations
Kruskal version (sort edges + DSU)
Sort all edges by cost and take an edge whenever it joins two different components.
public int minCostConnectPoints(int[][] points) {    int n = points.length;    List<int[]> edges = new ArrayList<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++)            edges.add(new int[]{Math.abs(points[i][0] - points[j][0]) + Math.abs(points[i][1] - points[j][1]), i, j});    edges.sort((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));    int[] parent = new int[n];    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) parent[i] = i;    int total = 0, used = 0;    for (int[] e : edges) {        int a = find(parent, e[1]), b = find(parent, e[2]);        if (a == b) continue;                                  // would close a cycle        parent[a] = b;        total += e[0];        if (++used == n - 1) break;    }    return total;}​private int find(int[] p, int x) {    while (p[x] != x) x = p[x] = p[p[x]];    return x;}
  • LC 1135 Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost (premium) — Kruskal on the given edges; −1 if not all joined.
LC 1976Number of Ways to Arrive at DestinationMediumDay 17 · #98
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalDijkstra + counting shortest paths
Spot itNumber of shortest paths from 0 to n − 1 (mod 10⁹+7).
“Strictly shorter: copy the ways. Equally short: add the ways.”
class Solution {    public int countPaths(int n, int[][] roads) {        final int MOD = 1_000_000_007;        List<List<int[]>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] r : roads) { g.get(r[0]).add(new int[]{r[1], r[2]}); g.get(r[1]).add(new int[]{r[0], r[2]}); }        long[] dist = new long[n], ways = new long[n];        Arrays.fill(dist, Long.MAX_VALUE);        dist[0] = 0;        ways[0] = 1;        PriorityQueue<long[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // long        pq.offer(new long[]{0, 0});        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {            long[] cur = pq.poll();            int u = (int) cur[0];            if (cur[1] > dist[u]) continue;            for (int[] e : g.get(u)) {                int v = e[0];                long nd = dist[u] + e[1];                if (nd < dist[v]) {                                 // shorter: reset                    dist[v] = nd;                    ways[v] = ways[u];                    pq.offer(new long[]{v, nd});                } else if (nd == dist[v]) {                         // tie: add                    ways[v] = (ways[v] + ways[u]) % MOD;                }            }        }        return (int) ways[n - 1];    }}
CostO(E log E) time · O(V + E) space
TrapDistances reach 2·10¹¹: use long for dist and for the heap entries.
LC 787Cheapest Flights Within K StopsMediumDay 17 · #99
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalBellman–Ford with a hop limit
Spot itCheapest flight from src to dst with at most k stops.
“k stops = k + 1 flights = k + 1 rounds; each round relaxes from LAST round's prices.”
class Solution {    public int findCheapestPrice(int n, int[][] flights, int src, int dst, int k) {        int[] cost = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(cost, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        cost[src] = 0;        for (int round = 0; round <= k; round++) {                           // k + 1 rounds            int[] next = cost.clone();                                       // copy            for (int[] f : flights) {                if (cost[f[0]] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) continue;                next[f[1]] = Math.min(next[f[1]], cost[f[0]] + f[2]);        // from the old prices            }            cost = next;        }        return cost[dst] == Integer.MAX_VALUE ? -1 : cost[dst];    }}
CostO(k · E) time · O(n) space
TrapWithout the copy (next = cost.clone()), one round can chain several flights and break the limit.
Variations
  • Dijkstra on (city, stops) — Also works; the state must include the stop count.

“Empty cell costs 0 (front of the deque), obstacle costs 1 (back).”
class Solution {    public int minimumObstacles(int[][] grid) {        int m = grid.length, n = grid[0].length;        int[][] dist = new int[m][n];        for (int[] row : dist) Arrays.fill(row, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        dist[0][0] = 0;        Deque<int[]> dq = new ArrayDeque<>();        dq.offerFirst(new int[]{0, 0});        int[] dr = {1, -1, 0, 0}, dc = {0, 0, 1, -1};        while (!dq.isEmpty()) {            int[] c = dq.pollFirst();            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {                int r = c[0] + dr[d], col = c[1] + dc[d];                if (r < 0 || col < 0 || r >= m || col >= n) continue;                int nd = dist[c[0]][c[1]] + grid[r][col];                if (nd < dist[r][col]) {                    dist[r][col] = nd;                    if (grid[r][col] == 0) dq.offerFirst(new int[]{r, col});                    else dq.offerLast(new int[]{r, col});                }            }        }        return dist[m - 1][n - 1];    }}
CostO(m·n) time · O(m·n) space
TrapThe cost belongs to the cell you ENTER.
LC 2421Number of Good PathsHardDay 17 · #101
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalDSU in value order
Spot itCount paths whose two ends have the same value and no node on the path is bigger.
“Add nodes from small to large; join a neighbour only if it is not bigger; count equal values per component.”
class Solution {    public int numberOfGoodPaths(int[] vals, int[][] edges) {        int n = vals.length;        int[] parent = new int[n];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) parent[i] = i;        List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }        Integer[] order = new Integer[n];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) order[i] = i;        Arrays.sort(order, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(vals[a], vals[b]));           // small values first        int ans = n;                                                               // single nodes        for (int i = 0; i < n; ) {            int j = i;            while (j < n && vals[order[j]] == vals[order[i]]) j++;            for (int t = i; t < j; t++)                for (int v : g.get(order[t]))                    if (vals[v] <= vals[order[t]]) union(parent, order[t], v);     // only not-bigger neighbours            Map<Integer, Integer> perRoot = new HashMap<>();            for (int t = i; t < j; t++) perRoot.merge(find(parent, order[t]), 1, Integer::sum);            for (int c : perRoot.values()) ans += c * (c - 1) / 2;                 // pairs in one component            i = j;        }        return ans;    }​    private int find(int[] p, int x) {        while (p[x] != x) x = p[x] = p[p[x]];        return x;    }​    private void union(int[] p, int a, int b) { p[find(p, a)] = find(p, b); }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapProcess ALL nodes of one value (all their unions) before counting pairs for that value.
Variations
  • LC 684 Redundant Connection — DSU over the edges; the first edge whose ends are already joined is the answer.
Day 18

Trees I: recursion, parent arrays, LCA

LeetCode TreeNode recursion, general trees without recursion, and binary lifting.

plan date Tue 24 Nov
learn these cards Wed 2 Dec
Pattern coreTrees without recursion: BFS order from a parent array or an edge list
Infosys trees arrive as parent[] or as edges, with n up to 10⁵ — deep recursion can overflow Java's stack. Get a BFS order once; walking it BACKWARDS visits children before parents (sizes, tree DP), walking it forwards visits parents first (depths, rerooting).
static int[] bfsOrderFromEdges(int n, int[][] edges, int root, int[] parentOut) {    List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());    for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }    int[] order = new int[n];    Arrays.fill(parentOut, -1);    boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];    int head = 0, tail = 0;    order[tail++] = root;    seen[root] = true;    while (head < tail) {        int u = order[head++];        for (int v : g.get(u)) if (!seen[v]) { seen[v] = true; parentOut[v] = u; order[tail++] = v; }    }    return order;}​static int[] subtreeSizes(int[] order, int[] parent) {    int[] size = new int[order.length];    for (int i = order.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {       // children before parents        int v = order[i];        size[v] += 1;        if (parent[v] != -1) size[parent[v]] += size[v];    }    return size;}
LC 543Diameter of Binary TreeEasyDay 18 · #102
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalPost-order · bend at a node
Spot itLongest path (in edges) between any two nodes of a binary tree.
“Each node returns its height; the path bending here is left + right.”
class Solution {    private int best = 0;​    public int diameterOfBinaryTree(TreeNode root) {        best = 0;        height(root);        return best;    }​    private int height(TreeNode node) {                    // nodes on the longest downward path        if (node == null) return 0;        int l = height(node.left), r = height(node.right);        best = Math.max(best, l + r);                      // bend here        return 1 + Math.max(l, r);                         // one side goes up    }}
CostO(n) time · O(h) space
TrapReturn 1 + max(l, r) to the parent, but record l + r in the global best.
Variations
LC 687 · Longest Univalue Path
The same shape; an arm only continues into a child with the same value.
private int best;​public int longestUnivaluePath(TreeNode root) {    best = 0;    arm(root);    return best;}​private int arm(TreeNode n) {    if (n == null) return 0;    int l = arm(n.left), r = arm(n.right);    l = n.left != null && n.left.val == n.val ? l + 1 : 0;    r = n.right != null && n.right.val == n.val ? r + 1 : 0;    best = Math.max(best, l + r);    return Math.max(l, r);}
LC 236Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary TreeMediumDay 18 · #103
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalLCA by recursion
Spot itLowest common ancestor of p and q in a binary tree.
“Return what you found; if both sides found something, you are the answer.”
class Solution {    public TreeNode lowestCommonAncestor(TreeNode root, TreeNode p, TreeNode q) {        if (root == null || root == p || root == q) return root;        TreeNode l = lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q);        TreeNode r = lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q);        if (l != null && r != null) return root;                          // split here        return l != null ? l : r;                                         // pass it up    }}
CostO(n) time · O(h) space
TrapIf root is p (or q), return it at once: the other one is below it or the answer is above.
Variations
LC 235 · LCA of a Binary Search Tree
Values guide you: both smaller go left, both bigger go right, otherwise this node is the split.
public TreeNode lowestCommonAncestor(TreeNode root, TreeNode p, TreeNode q) {    TreeNode cur = root;    while (true) {        if (p.val < cur.val && q.val < cur.val) cur = cur.left;        else if (p.val > cur.val && q.val > cur.val) cur = cur.right;        else return cur;    }}

LC 124Binary Tree Maximum Path SumHardDay 18 · #104
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalPost-order · drop negative branches
Spot itMaximum path sum between any two nodes (values may be negative).
“Gain of a side is never below zero; the path bends here with both gains.”
class Solution {    private int best;​    public int maxPathSum(TreeNode root) {        best = Integer.MIN_VALUE;        gain(root);        return best;    }​    private int gain(TreeNode node) {        if (node == null) return 0;        int l = Math.max(0, gain(node.left));              // drop negatives        int r = Math.max(0, gain(node.right));        best = Math.max(best, node.val + l + r);           // bend here        return node.val + Math.max(l, r);                  // one side goes up    }}
CostO(n) time · O(h) space
TrapStart best at Integer.MIN_VALUE: a tree of only negatives must return its largest value.
LC 2246Longest Path With Different Adjacent CharactersHardDay 18 · #105
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalParent array · children before parents
Spot itLongest path where neighbouring nodes have different letters; the tree is a parent array.
“Keep the two longest child chains with a different letter; the path bends at the node.”
class Solution {    public int longestPath(int[] parent, String s) {        int n = parent.length;        int[] pending = new int[n];                        // children not processed yet        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) pending[parent[i]]++;        int[] best1 = new int[n], best2 = new int[n];      // two longest usable child chains        Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (pending[i] == 0) q.offer(i);   // leaves first        int ans = 1;        while (!q.isEmpty()) {            int v = q.poll();            int down = 1 + best1[v];            ans = Math.max(ans, 1 + best1[v] + best2[v]);             // bend at v            int p = parent[v];            if (p == -1) continue;            if (s.charAt(p) != s.charAt(v)) {                         // only different letters join                if (down > best1[p]) { best2[p] = best1[p]; best1[p] = down; }                else if (down > best2[p]) best2[p] = down;            }            if (--pending[p] == 0) q.offer(p);        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
Trapn is 10⁵: no recursion. Process leaves first (a counter of unfinished children per node).
Variations
Tree diameter from an edge list: BFS twice (LC 1245, premium)
BFS from any node; the farthest node is one end of a diameter. BFS again from it; the farthest distance is the diameter.
public int treeDiameter(int[][] edges) {    int n = edges.length + 1;    List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());    for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }    int[] first = farthest(g, 0);    return farthest(g, first[0])[1];}​private int[] farthest(List<List<Integer>> g, int src) {   // {node, distance}    int[] dist = new int[g.size()];    Arrays.fill(dist, -1);    dist[src] = 0;    Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();    q.offer(src);    int last = src;    while (!q.isEmpty()) {        int u = q.poll();        last = u;        for (int v : g.get(u)) if (dist[v] == -1) { dist[v] = dist[u] + 1; q.offer(v); }    }    return new int[]{last, dist[last]};}
LC 102Binary Tree Level Order TraversalMediumDay 18 · #106
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalBFS by levels
Spot itValues of a binary tree level by level.
“Freeze q.size(): that many nodes are this level.”
class Solution {    public List<List<Integer>> levelOrder(TreeNode root) {        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();        if (root == null) return res;        Deque<TreeNode> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        q.offer(root);        while (!q.isEmpty()) {            List<Integer> level = new ArrayList<>();            for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {          // one level                TreeNode node = q.poll();                level.add(node.val);                if (node.left != null) q.offer(node.left);                if (node.right != null) q.offer(node.right);            }            res.add(level);        }        return res;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapRead q.size() ONCE before the inner loop; it changes as you push children.
Variations
LC 199 · Binary Tree Right Side View
The same level loop; keep only the last node of each level.
public List<Integer> rightSideView(TreeNode root) {    List<Integer> res = new ArrayList<>();    if (root == null) return res;    Deque<TreeNode> q = new ArrayDeque<>();    q.offer(root);    while (!q.isEmpty()) {        for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {            TreeNode node = q.poll();            if (size == 1) res.add(node.val);            if (node.left != null) q.offer(node.left);            if (node.right != null) q.offer(node.right);        }    }    return res;}

Spot itMany queries "k-th ancestor of node".
“Store the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th … ancestor; jump by the set bits of k.”
class TreeAncestor {    private static final int LOG = 16;                     // 2^16 > 5·10^4    private final int[][] up;                              // up[j][v] = 2^j-th ancestor​    public TreeAncestor(int n, int[] parent) {        up = new int[LOG][];        up[0] = parent.clone();        for (int j = 1; j < LOG; j++) {            up[j] = new int[n];            for (int v = 0; v < n; v++)                up[j][v] = up[j - 1][v] == -1 ? -1 : up[j - 1][up[j - 1][v]];   // 2^j = 2^(j-1) twice        }    }​    public int getKthAncestor(int node, int k) {        for (int j = 0; j < LOG && node != -1; j++)            if (((k >> j) & 1) == 1) node = up[j][node];                       // jump by set bits        return node;    }}
CostO(n log n) build · O(log n) per query
TrapUse −1 for "no ancestor" and stop as soon as the node becomes −1.
LC 2477Minimum Fuel Cost to Report to the CapitalMediumDay 18 · #108
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalSubtree sizes
Spot itEvery city sends one representative to the capital; cars have seats; minimise litres of fuel.
“The edge above a subtree of size s carries s people, so it needs ceil(s / seats) cars.”
class Solution {    public long minimumFuelCost(int[][] roads, int seats) {        int n = roads.length + 1;        List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] r : roads) { g.get(r[0]).add(r[1]); g.get(r[1]).add(r[0]); }        int[] order = new int[n], parent = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(parent, -1);        boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];        int head = 0, tail = 0;        order[tail++] = 0;        seen[0] = true;        while (head < tail) {            int u = order[head++];            for (int v : g.get(u)) if (!seen[v]) { seen[v] = true; parent[v] = u; order[tail++] = v; }        }        long[] size = new long[n];        long fuel = 0;        for (int i = n - 1; i > 0; i--) {                          // children first, skip the root            int v = order[i];            size[v] += 1;            fuel += (size[v] + seats - 1) / seats;                 // cars on the edge above v            size[parent[v]] += size[v];        }        return fuel;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapThe answer can exceed 2³¹: return a long.
LC 2846Minimum Edge Weight Equilibrium Queries in a TreeHardDay 18 · #109
learn Wed 2Thu 3finalLCA + counts on root paths
Spot itFor each query path, fewest edge weight changes to make all weights equal (weights 1..26).
“Count each weight from the root; path count = cnt[a] + cnt[b] − 2·cnt[lca]. Keep the most common, change the rest.”
class Solution {    private static final int LOG = 15;                             // 2^14 > 10^4    private int[][] up;    private int[] depth;​    public int[] minOperationsQueries(int n, int[][] edges, int[][] queries) {        List<List<int[]>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(new int[]{e[1], e[2]}); g.get(e[1]).add(new int[]{e[0], e[2]}); }        up = new int[LOG][n];        depth = new int[n];        int[][] cnt = new int[n][27];                              // cnt[v][w] = edges of weight w on root..v        boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];        Deque<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        q.offer(0);        seen[0] = true;        while (!q.isEmpty()) {            int u = q.poll();            for (int[] e : g.get(u)) {                int v = e[0];                if (seen[v]) continue;                seen[v] = true;                up[0][v] = u;                depth[v] = depth[u] + 1;                cnt[v] = cnt[u].clone();                cnt[v][e[1]]++;                q.offer(v);            }        }        for (int j = 1; j < LOG; j++)            for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) up[j][v] = up[j - 1][up[j - 1][v]];   // the root points to itself        int[] ans = new int[queries.length];        for (int i = 0; i < queries.length; i++) {            int a = queries[i][0], b = queries[i][1], l = lca(a, b), most = 0;            for (int w = 1; w <= 26; w++) most = Math.max(most, cnt[a][w] + cnt[b][w] - 2 * cnt[l][w]);            ans[i] = depth[a] + depth[b] - 2 * depth[l] - most;        }        return ans;    }​    private int lca(int a, int b) {        if (depth[a] < depth[b]) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }        int diff = depth[a] - depth[b];        for (int j = 0; j < LOG; j++) if (((diff >> j) & 1) == 1) a = up[j][a];   // same depth        if (a == b) return a;        for (int j = LOG - 1; j >= 0; j--)            if (up[j][a] != up[j][b]) { a = up[j][a]; b = up[j][b]; }             // climb together        return up[0][a];    }}
CostO((n + q) · (log n + 26)) time · O(26 · n) space
TrapPath length is depth[a] + depth[b] − 2·depth[lca]; the answer is that minus the most frequent weight.
Day 19

Trees II: tree DP, rerooting, small-to-large

dp[v][state] from the children, answers for every root in O(n), and merging the smaller set into the larger.

plan date Wed 25 Nov
learn these cards Wed 25 Nov
Pattern coreTree DP and rerooting, both without recursion
Tree DP: walk the BFS order backwards and fold each child into its parent (dp[v][state]). Rerooting: first compute the answer for root 0; then walk the BFS order forwards and move the root across each edge, fixing only what that edge changes.
static long maxIndependentSet(int n, int[][] edges, int[] w) {   // no two chosen nodes adjacent    List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());    for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }    int[] order = new int[n], parent = new int[n];    Arrays.fill(parent, -1);    boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];    int head = 0, tail = 0;    order[tail++] = 0;    seen[0] = true;    while (head < tail) {        int u = order[head++];        for (int v : g.get(u)) if (!seen[v]) { seen[v] = true; parent[v] = u; order[tail++] = v; }    }    long[] take = new long[n], skip = new long[n];    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {                 // children first        int v = order[i];        take[v] += w[v];        int p = parent[v];        if (p == -1) continue;        take[p] += skip[v];                            // p taken: v must be skipped        skip[p] += Math.max(take[v], skip[v]);         // p skipped: v is free    }    return Math.max(take[0], skip[0]);}
LC 337House Robber IIIMediumDay 19 · #110
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Tree DP · two states
Spot itRob nodes of a binary tree, never two directly linked.
“Each node returns a pair: best if I am robbed, best if I am not.”
class Solution {    public int rob(TreeNode root) {        int[] r = best(root);        return Math.max(r[0], r[1]);    }​    private int[] best(TreeNode node) {                    // {robbed, not robbed}        if (node == null) return new int[]{0, 0};        int[] l = best(node.left), r = best(node.right);        int robbed = node.val + l[1] + r[1];               // children must rest        int skipped = Math.max(l[0], l[1]) + Math.max(r[0], r[1]);   // children choose        return new int[]{robbed, skipped};    }}
CostO(n) time · O(h) space
TrapIf this node is NOT robbed, each child picks its own better state (not necessarily "robbed").
Variations
LC 968 · Binary Tree Cameras (three states)
Return 0 = not covered, 1 = covered, 2 = has a camera. A child that is not covered forces a camera here. Check the root at the end.
private int cams;​public int minCameraCover(TreeNode root) {    cams = 0;    return state(root) == 0 ? cams + 1 : cams;}​private int state(TreeNode n) {    if (n == null) return 1;    int l = state(n.left), r = state(n.right);    if (l == 0 || r == 0) { cams++; return 2; }    if (l == 2 || r == 2) return 1;    return 0;}
LC 1519Number of Nodes in the Sub-Tree With the Same LabelMediumDay 19 · #111
