Spot itFor each node, how many nodes in its subtree share its label?
“Every node keeps 26 counters; children add theirs to the parent.”
class Solution {    public int[] countSubTrees(int n, int[][] edges, String labels) {        List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }        int[] order = new int[n], parent = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(parent, -1);        boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];        int head = 0, tail = 0;        order[tail++] = 0;        seen[0] = true;        while (head < tail) {                                            // root it at 0            int u = order[head++];            for (int v : g.get(u)) if (!seen[v]) { seen[v] = true; parent[v] = u; order[tail++] = v; }        }        int[][] cnt = new int[n][26];        int[] ans = new int[n];        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {                               // children first            int v = order[i];            ans[v] = ++cnt[v][labels.charAt(v) - 'a'];            if (parent[v] != -1)                for (int c = 0; c < 26; c++) cnt[parent[v]][c] += cnt[v][c];   // merge into parent        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(26 · n) time · O(26 · n) space
TrapThe edges are undirected: root the tree at 0 with a BFS first.
LC 834Sum of Distances in TreeHardDay 19 · #112
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Rerooting
Spot itFor every node, the sum of distances to all other nodes.
“Moving the root to a child brings size[child] nodes one closer and the other n − size[child] one farther.”
class Solution {    public int[] sumOfDistancesInTree(int n, int[][] edges) {        List<List<Integer>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }        int[] order = new int[n], parent = new int[n], depth = new int[n], size = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(parent, -1);        boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];        int head = 0, tail = 0;        order[tail++] = 0;        seen[0] = true;        while (head < tail) {            int u = order[head++];            for (int v : g.get(u)) if (!seen[v]) { seen[v] = true; parent[v] = u; depth[v] = depth[u] + 1; order[tail++] = v; }        }        int[] ans = new int[n];        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {                       // pass 1: sizes, ans[0]            int v = order[i];            size[v]++;            ans[0] += depth[v];            if (parent[v] != -1) size[parent[v]] += size[v];        }        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {                            // pass 2: parents first            int v = order[i];            ans[v] = ans[parent[v]] - size[v] + (n - size[v]);        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapCompute ans[0] (sum of depths) and all subtree sizes BEFORE the forward pass.
LC 3068Find the Maximum Sum of Node ValuesHardDay 19 · #113
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Parity trick (tree shape does not matter)
Spot itOperation: pick an edge and XOR both ends with k. Maximise the sum.
“Repeating along paths lets you flip ANY even number of nodes: take every gain, fix the parity once.”
class Solution {    public long maximumValueSum(int[] nums, int k, int[][] edges) {        long sum = 0;        int flips = 0, minLoss = Integer.MAX_VALUE;        for (int x : nums) {            int y = x ^ k;            sum += Math.max(x, y);                                // take the better value            if (y > x) flips++;            minLoss = Math.min(minLoss, Math.abs(y - x));        }        return flips % 2 == 0 ? sum : sum - minLoss;              // fix odd parity    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapIf an odd number of nodes want flipping, pay the smallest |x ^ k − x| once.
Variations
  • Tree DP version — dp[v][parity of flipped nodes in the subtree] gives the same answer.
LC 2858Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is ReachableHardDay 19 · #114
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Rerooting over edge directions
Spot itFor every node, fewest edge reversals so it can reach every other node.
“Count reversals from root 0; crossing an edge to the child changes the total by exactly ±1.”
class Solution {    public int[] minEdgeReversals(int n, int[][] edges) {        List<List<int[]>> g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) {            g.get(e[0]).add(new int[]{e[1], 0});                       // along the arrow            g.get(e[1]).add(new int[]{e[0], 1});                       // against it        }        int[] order = new int[n], parent = new int[n], costDown = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(parent, -1);        boolean[] seen = new boolean[n];        int head = 0, tail = 0, base = 0;        order[tail++] = 0;        seen[0] = true;        while (head < tail) {            int u = order[head++];            for (int[] e : g.get(u))                if (!seen[e[0]]) {                    seen[e[0]] = true;                    parent[e[0]] = u;                    costDown[e[0]] = e[1];                               // cost to go parent -> child                    base += e[1];                                        // reversals for root 0                    order[tail++] = e[0];                }        }        int[] ans = new int[n];        ans[0] = base;        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {            int v = order[i];            ans[v] = ans[parent[v]] + (costDown[v] == 0 ? 1 : -1);      // the edge flips its role        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapStore each edge both ways: cost 0 along its direction, cost 1 against it.
LC 2003Smallest Missing Genetic Value in Each SubtreeHardDay 19 · #115
learn Wed 25Thu 26Sat 28Thu 3Only one path matters
Spot itFor every subtree, the smallest missing genetic value (values are distinct, ≥ 1).
“A subtree without the value 1 answers 1; only the path from "the node with 1" up to the root needs work.”
class Solution {    public int[] smallestMissingValueSubtree(int[] parents, int[] nums) {        int n = parents.length;        int[] ans = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(ans, 1);                                          // most subtrees miss 1        int start = -1;        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (nums[i] == 1) start = i;        if (start == -1) return ans;        List<List<Integer>> children = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) children.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) children.get(parents[i]).add(i);        boolean[] visited = new boolean[n];        boolean[] has = new boolean[100_002];        int missing = 1;        for (int v = start; v != -1; v = parents[v]) {                // walk up from the 1            Deque<Integer> st = new ArrayDeque<>();            st.push(v);            while (!st.isEmpty()) {                                   // add the new part of the subtree                int u = st.pop();                if (visited[u]) continue;                visited[u] = true;                has[nums[u]] = true;                for (int c : children.get(u)) if (!visited[c]) st.push(c);            }            while (has[missing]) missing++;                           // only moves forward            ans[v] = missing;        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n + V) time · O(n + V) space
TrapDo not re-walk the branch you came from: a visited array makes the whole walk O(n).
Day 20

Fenwick trees and segment trees

Point updates with range queries for sum, min and gcd, coordinate compression, and Euler tours.

plan date Thu 26 Nov
learn these cards Thu 26 Nov
Pattern coreFenwick tree and iterative segment tree
Fenwick (1-indexed): add climbs with i += i & -i, prefix falls with i -= i & -i. Segment tree (iterative, size n): leaves at n + i, parent of p is p / 2; query walks l and r inward on a half-open range [l, r).
static final class Fenwick {    final long[] t;​    Fenwick(int n) { t = new long[n + 1]; }​    void add(int i, long v) { for (i++; i < t.length; i += i & -i) t[i] += v; }   // 0-indexed i​    long prefix(int i) { long s = 0; for (; i > 0; i -= i & -i) s += t[i]; return s; }   // sum of [0, i)​    long range(int l, int r) { return prefix(r + 1) - prefix(l); }                 // sum of [l, r]}​static final class MaxSegTree {    final int n;    final int[] t;​    MaxSegTree(int n) { this.n = n; t = new int[2 * n]; }​    void set(int i, int v) {        for (t[i += n] = v; i > 1; i >>= 1) t[i >> 1] = Math.max(t[i], t[i ^ 1]);    }​    int max(int l, int r) {                         // max on [l, r), 0 if empty        int res = 0;        for (l += n, r += n; l < r; l >>= 1, r >>= 1) {            if ((l & 1) == 1) res = Math.max(res, t[l++]);            if ((r & 1) == 1) res = Math.max(res, t[--r]);        }        return res;    }}
LC 307Range Sum Query - MutableMediumDay 20 · #116
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Fenwick tree
Spot itPoint updates and range sums, mixed together.
“Store the difference on update; a range is prefix(r + 1) − prefix(l).”
class NumArray {    private final int n;    private final int[] nums, tree;                       // tree is 1-indexed​    public NumArray(int[] nums) {        n = nums.length;        this.nums = new int[n];        tree = new int[n + 1];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) update(i, nums[i]);    }​    public void update(int index, int val) {        int delta = val - nums[index];        nums[index] = val;        for (int i = index + 1; i <= n; i += i & -i) tree[i] += delta;   // climb    }​    public int sumRange(int left, int right) {        return prefix(right + 1) - prefix(left);    }​    private int prefix(int i) {                           // sum of the first i numbers        int s = 0;        for (; i > 0; i -= i & -i) s += tree[i];          // fall        return s;    }}
CostO(log n) per operation · O(n) space
Trapupdate SETS a value: add val − nums[index] and remember the new value.
Variations
Segment tree version (iterative, also gives min / max / gcd)
Swap + for Math.max, Math.min or gcd and the same code answers range max / min / gcd (CF 914D uses gcd).
class NumArray {    private final int n;    private final int[] t;​    public NumArray(int[] nums) {        n = nums.length;        t = new int[2 * n];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) t[n + i] = nums[i];        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 1; i--) t[i] = t[2 * i] + t[2 * i + 1];    }​    public void update(int index, int val) {        int p = index + n;        t[p] = val;        for (p >>= 1; p >= 1; p >>= 1) t[p] = t[2 * p] + t[2 * p + 1];    }​    public int sumRange(int left, int right) {        int s = 0;        for (int l = left + n, r = right + n + 1; l < r; l >>= 1, r >>= 1) {            if ((l & 1) == 1) s += t[l++];            if ((r & 1) == 1) s += t[--r];        }        return s;    }}
LC 315Count of Smaller Numbers After SelfHardDay 20 · #117
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Fenwick over compressed values
Spot itFor each element, how many smaller elements are to its right?
“Walk from the right; ask the tree how many smaller values it has seen, then add yourself.”
class Solution {    public List<Integer> countSmaller(int[] nums) {        int n = nums.length;        int[] sorted = nums.clone();        Arrays.sort(sorted);        int[] tree = new int[n + 1];        Integer[] ans = new Integer[n];        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {            int rank = Arrays.binarySearch(sorted, nums[i]);         // some index of nums[i]            while (rank > 0 && sorted[rank - 1] == nums[i]) rank--;  // first index = count of smaller values            int c = 0;            for (int j = rank; j > 0; j -= j & -j) c += tree[j];     // seen values with rank < mine            ans[i] = c;            for (int j = rank + 1; j <= n; j += j & -j) tree[j]++;   // add myself at rank + 1        }        return Arrays.asList(ans);    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapCompress values to ranks 1..m first (they can be negative); query rank − 1 for STRICTLY smaller.
Variations
Count inversions with merge sort (GfG, also LC 493 Reverse Pairs)
While merging, every time the right half wins, all remaining left elements form inversions with it. For LC 493 count a[i] > 2L·a[j] with a separate pointer before merging.
static long inversions(int[] a) {    return sort(a.clone(), new int[a.length], 0, a.length - 1);}​private static long sort(int[] a, int[] tmp, int lo, int hi) {    if (lo >= hi) return 0;    int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;    long cnt = sort(a, tmp, lo, mid) + sort(a, tmp, mid + 1, hi);    int i = lo, j = mid + 1, k = lo;    while (i <= mid && j <= hi) {        if (a[i] <= a[j]) tmp[k++] = a[i++];        else { cnt += mid - i + 1; tmp[k++] = a[j++]; }   // a[i..mid] are all > a[j]    }    while (i <= mid) tmp[k++] = a[i++];    while (j <= hi) tmp[k++] = a[j++];    System.arraycopy(tmp, lo, a, lo, hi - lo + 1);    return cnt;}
LC 2407Longest Increasing Subsequence IIHardDay 20 · #118
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4LIS with a segment tree over values
Spot itLongest strictly increasing subsequence where neighbours differ by at most k.
“Best chain ending at value x = 1 + max over values in [x − k, x − 1]; a max segment tree answers that.”
class Solution {    public int lengthOfLIS(int[] nums, int k) {        int size = 100_001;                                      // values are 1..10^5        int[] t = new int[2 * size];        int best = 0;        for (int x : nums) {            int res = 0;            for (int l = Math.max(0, x - k) + size, r = x + size; l < r; l >>= 1, r >>= 1) {   // max on [x-k, x)                if ((l & 1) == 1) res = Math.max(res, t[l++]);                if ((r & 1) == 1) res = Math.max(res, t[--r]);            }            int cur = res + 1;                                   // extend the best chain            best = Math.max(best, cur);            int p = x + size;            if (cur > t[p]) {                for (t[p] = cur; p > 1; p >>= 1) t[p >> 1] = Math.max(t[p], t[p ^ 1]);   // point update            }        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n log V) time · O(V) space
TrapQuery BEFORE updating x, and the range is half-open in this tree: [x − k, x).
LC 2286Booking Concert Tickets in GroupsHardDay 20 · #119
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Segment tree (max + sum) with descent
Spot itn rows of m seats; gather k together in the first row ≤ maxRow that fits, or scatter k anywhere in rows ≤ maxRow.
“Max finds the first row with room by walking down the tree; sum answers "enough seats in total?".”
class BookMyShow {    private final int n, m;    private final long[] sum;    private final int[] max, free;    private int firstFree = 0;​    public BookMyShow(int n, int m) {        this.n = n;        this.m = m;        sum = new long[4 * n];        max = new int[4 * n];        free = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(free, m);        build(1, 0, n - 1);    }​    public int[] gather(int k, int maxRow) {        int row = firstRow(1, 0, n - 1, k, maxRow);        if (row == -1) return new int[0];        int seat = m - free[row];        set(1, 0, n - 1, row, free[row] - k);        return new int[]{row, seat};    }​    public boolean scatter(int k, int maxRow) {        if (total(1, 0, n - 1, maxRow) < k) return false;        while (k > 0) {            int take = Math.min(free[firstFree], k);            set(1, 0, n - 1, firstFree, free[firstFree] - take);            k -= take;            if (free[firstFree] == 0) firstFree++;                     // never look back        }        return true;    }​    private void build(int node, int lo, int hi) {        if (lo == hi) { sum[node] = m; max[node] = m; return; }        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        build(2 * node, lo, mid);        build(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi);        sum[node] = sum[2 * node] + sum[2 * node + 1];        max[node] = Math.max(max[2 * node], max[2 * node + 1]);    }​    private void set(int node, int lo, int hi, int pos, int val) {        if (lo == hi) { free[pos] = val; sum[node] = val; max[node] = val; return; }        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        if (pos <= mid) set(2 * node, lo, mid, pos, val);        else set(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, pos, val);        sum[node] = sum[2 * node] + sum[2 * node + 1];        max[node] = Math.max(max[2 * node], max[2 * node + 1]);    }​    private int firstRow(int node, int lo, int hi, int k, int maxRow) {   // first row <= maxRow with >= k free        if (lo > maxRow || max[node] < k) return -1;                     // prune        if (lo == hi) return lo;        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        int r = firstRow(2 * node, lo, mid, k, maxRow);                  // try the left first        return r != -1 ? r : firstRow(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, k, maxRow);    }​    private long total(int node, int lo, int hi, int maxRow) {           // free seats in rows 0..maxRow        if (lo > maxRow) return 0;        if (hi <= maxRow) return sum[node];        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        return total(2 * node, lo, mid, maxRow) + total(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, maxRow);    }}
CostO(log n) per gather, amortised O(log n) per scatter
TrapScatter fills from the first non-full row; keep a pointer to it so full rows are never visited again.
LC 3165Maximum Sum of Subsequence With Non-adjacent ElementsHardDay 20 · #120
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Segment tree with 4 states per node
Spot itPoint updates, and after each one the best sum of non-adjacent elements (sum of answers mod 10⁹+7).
“Each node keeps the best for "may I use my first element / my last element"; joining needs one side of the seam to be unused.”
class Solution {    private long[][] t;                                   // t[node][f * 2 + l]: f / l = first / last element allowed​    public int maximumSumSubsequence(int[] nums, int[][] queries) {        int n = nums.length;        t = new long[4 * n][4];        build(1, 0, n - 1, nums);        long total = 0;        for (int[] q : queries) {            update(1, 0, n - 1, q[0], q[1]);            total = (total + t[1][3]) % 1_000_000_007L;   // root, both ends allowed        }        return (int) total;    }​    private void leaf(int node, int x) {        t[node][0] = t[node][1] = t[node][2] = 0;        t[node][3] = Math.max(0, x);                      // only "both allowed" may take it    }​    private void pull(int node) {        long[] L = t[2 * node], R = t[2 * node + 1];        for (int f = 0; f < 2; f++)            for (int l = 0; l < 2; l++)                t[node][f * 2 + l] = Math.max(L[f * 2] + R[2 + l], L[f * 2 + 1] + R[l]);   // seam: one side unused    }​    private void build(int node, int lo, int hi, int[] a) {        if (lo == hi) { leaf(node, a[lo]); return; }        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        build(2 * node, lo, mid, a);        build(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, a);        pull(node);    }​    private void update(int node, int lo, int hi, int pos, int x) {        if (lo == hi) { leaf(node, x); return; }        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        if (pos <= mid) update(2 * node, lo, mid, pos, x);        else update(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, pos, x);        pull(node);    }}
CostO((n + q) log n) time · O(n) space
TrapAn empty choice is allowed, so a negative leaf is worth 0, and sums need long.
LC 2322Minimum Score After Removals on a TreeHardDay 20 · #121
learn Thu 26Fri 27Sun 29Fri 4Euler tour · subtree inside subtree
Spot itRemove two edges from a tree; minimise (largest XOR − smallest XOR) of the three parts.
“An edge = the subtree under it. With entry/exit times you can tell if one subtree holds the other.”
class Solution {    private List<List<Integer>> g;    private int[] xr, tin, tout, nums;    private int timer;​    public int minimumScore(int[] nums, int[][] edges) {        int n = nums.length;        this.nums = nums;        g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (int[] e : edges) { g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]); g.get(e[1]).add(e[0]); }        xr = new int[n];        tin = new int[n];        tout = new int[n];        timer = 0;        dfs(0, -1);        int best = Integer.MAX_VALUE;        for (int u = 1; u < n; u++)                               // node u = the edge above u            for (int v = u + 1; v < n; v++) {                int a, b, c;                if (inside(v, u)) { a = xr[v]; b = xr[u] ^ xr[v]; c = xr[0] ^ xr[u]; }        // v under u                else if (inside(u, v)) { a = xr[u]; b = xr[v] ^ xr[u]; c = xr[0] ^ xr[v]; }   // u under v                else { a = xr[u]; b = xr[v]; c = xr[0] ^ xr[u] ^ xr[v]; }                     // separate                best = Math.min(best, Math.max(a, Math.max(b, c)) - Math.min(a, Math.min(b, c)));            }        return best;    }​    private boolean inside(int child, int anc) { return tin[anc] <= tin[child] && tout[child] <= tout[anc]; }​    private void dfs(int v, int p) {        tin[v] = timer++;        xr[v] = nums[v];        for (int w : g.get(v)) if (w != p) { dfs(w, v); xr[v] ^= xr[w]; }        tout[v] = timer++;    }}
CostO(n²) time · O(n) space
TrapIf v's subtree is inside u's, the three parts are x[v], x[u] ^ x[v] and total ^ x[u].
Day 21

Lazy segment trees and the K-parts DP

Range updates, then the split-into-K-parts DP that Infosys reuses for its hardest problems.

plan date Fri 27 Nov
learn these cards Fri 27 Nov
Pattern coreLazy segment tree: range add, range max
A node's lazy is an add that its children have not received yet. Push it down before you go into the children; pull the max back up after. This is the engine behind CF 833B "The Bakery" (the Infosys gift boxes) and CF 1527E.
static final class LazyMax {    final int n;    final long[] mx, lz;​    LazyMax(int n) { this.n = n; mx = new long[4 * n]; lz = new long[4 * n]; }​    void add(int l, int r, long v) { add(1, 0, n - 1, l, r, v); }       // add v to [l, r]​    long max(int l, int r) { return max(1, 0, n - 1, l, r); }           // max on [l, r]​    private void push(int node) {        for (int c = 2 * node; c <= 2 * node + 1; c++) { mx[c] += lz[node]; lz[c] += lz[node]; }        lz[node] = 0;    }​    private void add(int node, int lo, int hi, int l, int r, long v) {        if (r < lo || hi < l) return;        if (l <= lo && hi <= r) { mx[node] += v; lz[node] += v; return; }        push(node);        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        add(2 * node, lo, mid, l, r, v);        add(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, l, r, v);        mx[node] = Math.max(mx[2 * node], mx[2 * node + 1]);    }​    private long max(int node, int lo, int hi, int l, int r) {        if (r < lo || hi < l) return Long.MIN_VALUE;        if (l <= lo && hi <= r) return mx[node];        push(node);        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        return Math.max(max(2 * node, lo, mid, l, r), max(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, l, r));    }}
LC 1335Minimum Difficulty of a Job ScheduleHardDay 21 · #122
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Split into k parts · dp[day][i]
Spot itSchedule jobs in order over d days (at least one per day); a day costs its hardest job; minimise the total.
“The last day starts at some j: best for j jobs in d − 1 days plus max(j..i−1).”
class Solution {    public int minDifficulty(int[] jobDifficulty, int d) {        int n = jobDifficulty.length;        if (n < d) return -1;        final int INF = 1_000_000_000;        int[][] dp = new int[d + 1][n + 1];                              // dp[day][i] = first i jobs in day days        for (int[] row : dp) Arrays.fill(row, INF);        dp[0][0] = 0;        for (int day = 1; day <= d; day++)            for (int i = day; i <= n; i++) {                int mx = 0;                for (int j = i - 1; j >= day - 1; j--) {                 // last day = jobs j..i-1                    mx = Math.max(mx, jobDifficulty[j]);                    if (dp[day - 1][j] < INF) dp[day][i] = Math.min(dp[day][i], dp[day - 1][j] + mx);                }            }        return dp[d][n];    }}
CostO(d · n²) time · O(d · n) space
TrapWalk j DOWNWARDS from i − 1 so the max of the last day grows as you go; fewer jobs than days → −1.
Variations
  • Same frame, other part costs — LC 410 (sum), LC 813 (average), CF 833B (distinct count, needs the lazy tree).
LC 813Largest Sum of AveragesMediumDay 21 · #123
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Split into k parts · averages
Spot itSplit into at most k groups and maximise the sum of the group averages.
“Same k-parts DP; a part's value is its average from prefix sums.”
class Solution {    public double largestSumOfAverages(int[] nums, int k) {        int n = nums.length;        double[] P = new double[n + 1];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) P[i + 1] = P[i] + nums[i];        double[][] dp = new double[k + 1][n + 1];        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) dp[1][i] = P[i] / i;                       // one group        for (int j = 2; j <= k; j++)            for (int i = j; i <= n; i++)                for (int p = j - 1; p < i; p++)                                 // last group = p..i-1                    dp[j][i] = Math.max(dp[j][i], dp[j - 1][p] + (P[i] - P[p]) / (i - p));        return dp[k][n];    }}
CostO(k · n²) time · O(k · n) space
TrapUse double all the way; more groups never hurt here, so dp[k][n] is the answer.
LC 2916Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares IIHardDay 21 · #124
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Lazy segment tree over start positions
Spot itSum over all subarrays of (number of distinct values)², n up to 10⁵.
“Extending r adds 1 to the distinct count of every start after the previous copy of nums[r]; (f + 1)² − f² = 2f + 1.”
class Solution {    private long[] sum, lz;​    public int sumCounts(int[] nums) {        int n = nums.length;        sum = new long[4 * n];        lz = new long[4 * n];        Map<Integer, Integer> last = new HashMap<>();        long squares = 0, total = 0;                     // squares = Σ f(l, r)² over l <= r        for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {            int p = last.getOrDefault(nums[r], -1);            squares += 2 * query(1, 0, n - 1, p + 1, r) + (r - p);     // Σ (2f + 1) over starts p+1..r            add(1, 0, n - 1, p + 1, r);                                // those starts gain one value            last.put(nums[r], r);            total = (total + squares) % 1_000_000_007L;        }        return (int) total;    }​    private void push(int node, int lo, int mid, int hi) {        if (lz[node] == 0) return;        sum[2 * node] += lz[node] * (mid - lo + 1);        lz[2 * node] += lz[node];        sum[2 * node + 1] += lz[node] * (hi - mid);        lz[2 * node + 1] += lz[node];        lz[node] = 0;    }​    private void add(int node, int lo, int hi, int l, int r) {        if (r < lo || hi < l) return;        if (l <= lo && hi <= r) { sum[node] += hi - lo + 1; lz[node]++; return; }        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        push(node, lo, mid, hi);        add(2 * node, lo, mid, l, r);        add(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, l, r);        sum[node] = sum[2 * node] + sum[2 * node + 1];    }​    private long query(int node, int lo, int hi, int l, int r) {        if (r < lo || hi < l) return 0;        if (l <= lo && hi <= r) return sum[node];        int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;        push(node, lo, mid, hi);        return query(2 * node, lo, mid, l, r) + query(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, l, r);    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapRead the range SUM before adding 1 to it; keep sums in long and take the mod only on the total.
LC 732My Calendar IIIHardDay 21 · #125
learn Fri 27Sat 28Mon 30Fri 4Sweep line on a TreeMap
Spot itAfter each booking, the largest number of bookings that overlap at one moment.
“+1 at start, −1 at end, walk in time order, remember the highest running count.”
class MyCalendarThree {    private final TreeMap<Integer, Integer> diff = new TreeMap<>();​    public MyCalendarThree() {}​    public int book(int startTime, int endTime) {        diff.merge(startTime, 1, Integer::sum);        diff.merge(endTime, -1, Integer::sum);        int active = 0, best = 0;        for (int v : diff.values()) best = Math.max(best, active += v);        return best;    }}
CostO(n) per booking (n ≤ 400) · O(n) space
TrapBookings are half-open: an end and a start at the same time do not overlap, and the TreeMap merge handles that.
Variations
Dynamic lazy segment tree over 0..10⁹ (O(log C) per booking)
Nodes are created only when touched (a HashMap keyed by node id). max = own add + best child, so no push-down is needed for "range add, global max".
class MyCalendarThree {    private final Map<Long, Integer> max = new HashMap<>(), add = new HashMap<>();​    public MyCalendarThree() {}​    public int book(int startTime, int endTime) {        update(1, 0, 1_000_000_000, startTime, endTime - 1);        return max.getOrDefault(1L, 0);    }​    private void update(long node, int lo, int hi, int l, int r) {        if (r < lo || hi < l) return;        if (l <= lo && hi <= r) {            add.merge(node, 1, Integer::sum);            max.merge(node, 1, Integer::sum);            return;        }        int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;        update(2 * node, lo, mid, l, r);        update(2 * node + 1, mid + 1, hi, l, r);        max.put(node, add.getOrDefault(node, 0) + Math.max(max.getOrDefault(2 * node, 0), max.getOrDefault(2 * node + 1, 0)));    }}
Day 22

Backtracking, bitmask DP, digit DP

Brute force for partial marks, dp[mask] for n ≤ 20, and counting numbers digit by digit.

plan date Sat 28 Nov
learn these cards Sat 28 Nov
Pattern coreBitmask loops and the digit-DP skeleton
n ≤ 20 → think bitmask. Subsets of mask: for (s = mask; s > 0; s = (s − 1) & mask). Digit DP: walk the digits of N left to right with a tight flag (still equal to N's prefix); memoise only the non-tight states. Count in [lo, hi] as f(hi) − f(lo − 1).
static int countSubmasks(int mask) {    int c = 1;                                        // the empty submask    for (int s = mask; s > 0; s = (s - 1) & mask) c++;    return c;}​private static char[] dig;private static long[][] memo;private static int mod;​static long countDigitSumDivisible(long n, int d) {   // x in [0, n] with digit sum % d == 0    dig = Long.toString(n).toCharArray();    mod = d;    memo = new long[dig.length][d];    for (long[] row : memo) Arrays.fill(row, -1);    return go(0, 0, true);}​private static long go(int pos, int rem, boolean tight) {    if (pos == dig.length) return rem == 0 ? 1 : 0;    if (!tight && memo[pos][rem] != -1) return memo[pos][rem];    int limit = tight ? dig[pos] - '0' : 9;    long res = 0;    for (int x = 0; x <= limit; x++) res += go(pos + 1, (rem + x) % mod, tight && x == limit);    if (!tight) memo[pos][rem] = res;    return res;}
LC 78SubsetsMediumDay 22 · #126
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Bitmask enumeration
Spot itAll subsets of distinct numbers.
“Every mask from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1 is one subset: bit i on means take nums[i].”
class Solution {    public List<List<Integer>> subsets(int[] nums) {        int n = nums.length;        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();        for (int mask = 0; mask < 1 << n; mask++) {            List<Integer> cur = new ArrayList<>();            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (((mask >> i) & 1) == 1) cur.add(nums[i]);            res.add(cur);        }        return res;    }}
CostO(n · 2ⁿ) time · O(n · 2ⁿ) output
TrapUse 1 << n subsets, including the empty one.
Variations
LC 90 · Subsets II (with duplicates): backtracking
Choose / skip recursion. Sort first; at one depth, skip a value equal to the previous one so each subset appears once.
public List<List<Integer>> subsetsWithDup(int[] nums) {    Arrays.sort(nums);    List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();    build(nums, 0, new ArrayList<>(), res);    return res;}​private void build(int[] a, int start, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {    res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur));                    // copy: cur keeps changing    for (int i = start; i < a.length; i++) {        if (i > start && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue;  // same value at the same depth        cur.add(a[i]);        build(a, i + 1, cur, res);        cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);                   // undo    }}
LC 46 · Permutations
Backtracking with a used[] array: try every unused number in the next position, then undo.
public List<List<Integer>> permute(int[] nums) {    List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();    build(nums, new boolean[nums.length], new ArrayList<>(), res);    return res;}​private void build(int[] a, boolean[] used, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {    if (cur.size() == a.length) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {        if (used[i]) continue;        used[i] = true;        cur.add(a[i]);        build(a, used, cur, res);        cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);        used[i] = false;    }}
LC 39 · Combination Sum (reuse allowed)
Same skeleton; recurse with i (not i + 1) to allow reuse, and stop when the remainder goes negative.
public List<List<Integer>> combinationSum(int[] candidates, int target) {    List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();    build(candidates, 0, target, new ArrayList<>(), res);    return res;}​private void build(int[] c, int start, int remain, List<Integer> cur, List<List<Integer>> res) {    if (remain == 0) { res.add(new ArrayList<>(cur)); return; }    for (int i = start; i < c.length; i++) {        if (c[i] > remain) continue;        cur.add(c[i]);        build(c, i, remain - c[i], cur, res);         // i again: reuse        cur.remove(cur.size() - 1);    }}
LC 1986Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the TasksMediumDay 22 · #127
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Bitmask DP with a pair state
Spot itFewest work sessions of length sessionTime to finish all tasks (n ≤ 14).
“For each set of done tasks, keep (sessions used, time in the last one) and compare in that order.”
class Solution {    public int minSessions(int[] tasks, int sessionTime) {        int n = tasks.length;        int[][] dp = new int[1 << n][];                                    // {sessions, time used in the last}        dp[0] = new int[]{1, 0};        for (int mask = 1; mask < 1 << n; mask++) {            int[] best = null;            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {                if (((mask >> i) & 1) == 0) continue;                int[] prev = dp[mask ^ (1 << i)];                           // task i was the last one added                int[] cand = prev[1] + tasks[i] <= sessionTime                        ? new int[]{prev[0], prev[1] + tasks[i]}            // fits in the open session                        : new int[]{prev[0] + 1, tasks[i]};                 // open a new session                if (best == null || cand[0] < best[0] || (cand[0] == best[0] && cand[1] < best[1])) best = cand;            }            dp[mask] = best;        }        return dp[(1 << n) - 1][0];    }}
CostO(n · 2ⁿ) time · O(2ⁿ) space
TrapStart from {1, 0}: one open, empty session.
Variations
  • LC 698 Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets — The same DP with sessionTime = total / k; answer is whether it fits in k.
LC 1879Minimum XOR Sum of Two ArraysHardDay 22 · #128
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Assignment bitmask DP
Spot itPair every nums1[i] with a distinct nums2[j]; minimise the sum of XORs (n ≤ 14).
“The mask says which nums2 are taken; its bit count says which nums1 is next.”
class Solution {    public int minimumXORSum(int[] nums1, int[] nums2) {        int n = nums1.length;        int[] dp = new int[1 << n];        Arrays.fill(dp, Integer.MAX_VALUE);        dp[0] = 0;        for (int mask = 0; mask < 1 << n; mask++) {            if (dp[mask] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) continue;            int i = Integer.bitCount(mask);                                   // next nums1 index            if (i == n) continue;            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)                if (((mask >> j) & 1) == 0)                    dp[mask | 1 << j] = Math.min(dp[mask | 1 << j], dp[mask] + (nums1[i] ^ nums2[j]));        }        return dp[(1 << n) - 1];    }}
CostO(n · 2ⁿ) time · O(2ⁿ) space
TrapDo not loop over i separately: i = Integer.bitCount(mask) is forced.
Variations
  • LC 1947 Maximum Compatibility Score Sum — The same DP with max and a score table.
LC 902Numbers At Most N Given Digit SetHardDay 22 · #129
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Digit counting (tight walk)
Spot itHow many numbers ≤ n can be written with the given digits?
“Shorter lengths are free: D^len. Same length: at each position count smaller digits × D^rest, continue only on an equal digit.”
class Solution {    public int atMostNGivenDigitSet(String[] digits, int n) {        String s = String.valueOf(n);        int L = s.length(), D = digits.length, count = 0;        int[] pow = new int[L + 1];        pow[0] = 1;        for (int i = 1; i <= L; i++) pow[i] = pow[i - 1] * D;        for (int len = 1; len < L; len++) count += pow[len];                // all shorter numbers        for (int i = 0; i < L; i++) {            char c = s.charAt(i);            int smaller = 0;            boolean equal = false;            for (String d : digits) {                if (d.charAt(0) < c) smaller++;                else if (d.charAt(0) == c) equal = true;            }            count += smaller * pow[L - i - 1];                              // smaller digit here: rest is free            if (!equal) return count;                                       // cannot stay tight        }        return count + 1;                                                   // n itself    }}
CostO(len · D) time · O(1) space
TrapIf every digit of n is available, n itself counts: add 1 at the end.
LC 51N-QueensHardDay 22 · #130
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Backtracking with flags
Spot itPlace n queens so none attack each other; list all boards.
“One queen per row; columns and both diagonals each get a "used" flag.”
class Solution {    public List<List<String>> solveNQueens(int n) {        List<List<String>> res = new ArrayList<>();        place(0, n, new int[n], new boolean[n], new boolean[2 * n], new boolean[2 * n], res);        return res;    }​    private void place(int r, int n, int[] colOf, boolean[] col, boolean[] d1, boolean[] d2, List<List<String>> res) {        if (r == n) {            List<String> board = new ArrayList<>();            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {                char[] row = new char[n];                Arrays.fill(row, '.');                row[colOf[i]] = 'Q';                board.add(new String(row));            }            res.add(board);            return;        }        for (int c = 0; c < n; c++) {            if (col[c] || d1[r + c] || d2[r - c + n - 1]) continue;            col[c] = d1[r + c] = d2[r - c + n - 1] = true;                              // place            colOf[r] = c;            place(r + 1, n, colOf, col, d1, d2, res);            col[c] = d1[r + c] = d2[r - c + n - 1] = false;                             // undo        }    }}
CostO(n!) time · O(n) space
TrapDiagonals: r + c for one direction, r − c + n − 1 for the other (shifted to stay ≥ 0).
Variations
LC 52 · N-Queens II with bitmasks
Three masks of attacked columns; shift the diagonal masks by one each row. free & -free picks the lowest free column.
public int totalNQueens(int n) {    return count(n, 0, 0, 0, 0);}​private int count(int n, int r, int cols, int d1, int d2) {    if (r == n) return 1;    int total = 0, free = ~(cols | d1 | d2) & ((1 << n) - 1);    while (free != 0) {        int bit = free & -free;        free -= bit;        total += count(n, r + 1, cols | bit, (d1 | bit) << 1, (d2 | bit) >> 1);    }    return total;}
  • LC 52 N-Queens II — Count only, no boards (code below with bitmasks).
LC 847Shortest Path Visiting All NodesHardDay 22 · #131
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4BFS over (node, visited mask)
Spot itShortest walk that visits every node (revisits allowed), n ≤ 12.
“The state is where you are plus who you have seen; start from every node at once.”
class Solution {    public int shortestPathLength(int[][] graph) {        int n = graph.length, full = (1 << n) - 1;        boolean[][] seen = new boolean[n][1 << n];        Deque<int[]> q = new ArrayDeque<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { q.offer(new int[]{i, 1 << i}); seen[i][1 << i] = true; }   // all starts        for (int steps = 0; !q.isEmpty(); steps++) {            for (int size = q.size(); size > 0; size--) {                int[] s = q.poll();                if (s[1] == full) return steps;                for (int v : graph[s[0]]) {                    int m = s[1] | 1 << v;                    if (!seen[v][m]) { seen[v][m] = true; q.offer(new int[]{v, m}); }                }            }        }        return 0;    }}
CostO(n² · 2ⁿ) time · O(n · 2ⁿ) space
TrapRevisits are allowed, so a plain node BFS is wrong; the mask makes states unique.
Variations
Shortest Hamiltonian path with weights (bitmask DP, TSP style)
dp[mask][v] = cheapest way to visit exactly mask and stand at v. Extend by one unvisited node at a time.
static long shortestHamiltonian(long[][] dist) {    int n = dist.length;    long INF = Long.MAX_VALUE / 4;    long[][] dp = new long[1 << n][n];    for (long[] row : dp) Arrays.fill(row, INF);    for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) dp[1 << v][v] = 0;    for (int mask = 1; mask < 1 << n; mask++)        for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) {            if (dp[mask][v] >= INF) continue;            for (int w = 0; w < n; w++)                if (((mask >> w) & 1) == 0)                    dp[mask | 1 << w][w] = Math.min(dp[mask | 1 << w][w], dp[mask][v] + dist[v][w]);        }    long best = INF;    for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) best = Math.min(best, dp[(1 << n) - 1][v]);    return best;}
LC 2827Number of Beautiful Integers in the RangeHardDay 22 · #132
learn Sat 28Sun 29Tue 1Fri 4Digit DP with several counters
Spot itCount numbers in [low, high] with as many even digits as odd digits and divisible by k.
“State = (position, even − odd, remainder, tight, started); answer f(high) − f(low − 1).”
class Solution {    private char[] d;    private int k;    private Integer[][][][] memo;​    public int numberOfBeautifulIntegers(int low, int high, int k) {        return count(high, k) - count(low - 1, k);    }​    private int count(int n, int k) {        if (n <= 0) return 0;        d = String.valueOf(n).toCharArray();        this.k = k;        memo = new Integer[d.length][21][k][2];        return go(0, 10, 0, true, false);                                   // diff offset by 10    }​    private int go(int pos, int diff, int rem, boolean tight, boolean started) {        if (pos == d.length) return started && diff == 10 && rem == 0 ? 1 : 0;        int s = started ? 1 : 0;        if (!tight && memo[pos][diff][rem][s] != null) return memo[pos][diff][rem][s];   // memo only when free        int limit = tight ? d[pos] - '0' : 9, res = 0;        for (int x = 0; x <= limit; x++) {            boolean st = started || x != 0;            int nd = st ? diff + (x % 2 == 0 ? 1 : -1) : diff;                         // leading zeros don't count            res += go(pos + 1, nd, (rem * 10 + x) % k, tight && x == limit, st);        }        if (!tight) memo[pos][diff][rem][s] = res;        return res;    }}
CostO(10 · 21 · k · 10) states × work · small
TrapLeading zeros are not digits: only count parity once started is true.

LC 881Boats to Save PeopleMediumDay 28 · #134
learn Thu 3Fri 4finalSort + two pointers
Spot itBoats hold at most two people and a weight limit; fewest boats.
“The heaviest always leaves; take the lightest with them if they fit.”
class Solution {    public int numRescueBoats(int[] people, int limit) {        Arrays.sort(people);        int boats = 0;        for (int l = 0, r = people.length - 1; l <= r; r--) {   // the heaviest leaves every time            if (people[l] + people[r] <= limit) l++;             // the lightest joins if they fit            boats++;        }        return boats;    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(1) space
TrapLoop while l <= r so the last single person also gets a boat.
LC 2300Successful Pairs of Spells and PotionsMediumDay 28 · #135
learn Thu 3Fri 4finalSort + lower bound
Spot itFor each spell, how many potions make spell × potion ≥ success?
“Sort potions; the first potion that works is a lower bound; everything after it works too.”
class Solution {    public int[] successfulPairs(int[] spells, int[] potions, long success) {        Arrays.sort(potions);        int m = potions.length;        int[] ans = new int[spells.length];        for (int i = 0; i < spells.length; i++) {            int lo = 0, hi = m;            while (lo < hi) {                int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;                if ((long) spells[i] * potions[mid] < success) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;            }            ans[i] = m - lo;        }        return ans;    }}
CostO((n + m) log m) time · O(1) extra
Trapspell * potion overflows int: compare in long.

LC 53Maximum SubarrayMediumBonus A · #137
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalKadane
Spot itLargest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
“Carry the run only while it helps: restart when the run is worse than the number alone.”
class Solution {    public int maxSubArray(int[] nums) {        int cur = nums[0], best = nums[0];        for (int i = 1; i < nums.length; i++) {            cur = Math.max(nums[i], cur + nums[i]);          // extend or restart            best = Math.max(best, cur);        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapStart best at nums[0], not 0: all numbers may be negative.
Variations
LC 918 · Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
A wrapping subarray = total − (a minimum subarray in the middle). Run Kadane for max and for min; if all are negative, return the plain max.
public int maxSubarraySumCircular(int[] nums) {    int total = 0, curMax = 0, curMin = 0, best = nums[0], worst = nums[0];    for (int x : nums) {        curMax = Math.max(x, curMax + x);        best = Math.max(best, curMax);        curMin = Math.min(x, curMin + x);        worst = Math.min(worst, curMin);        total += x;    }    return best < 0 ? best : Math.max(best, total - worst);}
  • Return the indices — Remember where the current run started when you restart.
LC 238Product of Array Except SelfMediumBonus A · #138
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalPrefix and suffix products
Spot itEach position gets the product of all other numbers, without division.
“Left products on the way in, right products on the way back.”
class Solution {    public int[] productExceptSelf(int[] nums) {        int n = nums.length;        int[] ans = new int[n];        ans[0] = 1;        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) ans[i] = ans[i - 1] * nums[i - 1];   // product of everything left        int right = 1;        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {            ans[i] *= right;                                            // times everything right            right *= nums[i];        }        return ans;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) extra (the output does not count)
TrapDivision breaks on zeros; this two-pass version never divides.
Variations
  • Same idea — LC 42 below (left max and right max) and LC 135 Candy (Day 4).
LC 128Longest Consecutive SequenceMediumBonus A · #139
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalHashSet · start only at run beginnings
Spot itLongest run of consecutive integers (any order) in O(n).
“Only start counting at x when x − 1 is missing; then walk up.”
class Solution {    public int longestConsecutive(int[] nums) {        Set<Integer> set = new HashSet<>();        for (int x : nums) set.add(x);        int best = 0;        for (int x : set) {            if (set.contains(x - 1)) continue;               // not a run start            int len = 1;            while (set.contains(x + len)) len++;             // walk up            best = Math.max(best, len);        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(n) space
TrapWithout the x − 1 check it becomes O(n²) on a long run.
LC 11Container With Most WaterMediumBonus A · #140
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalTwo pointers from both ends
Spot itTwo lines that hold the most water.
“Area is limited by the shorter line, so move the shorter one inward.”
class Solution {    public int maxArea(int[] height) {        int l = 0, r = height.length - 1, best = 0;        while (l < r) {            best = Math.max(best, Math.min(height[l], height[r]) * (r - l));            if (height[l] < height[r]) l++; else r--;                          // move the shorter        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapMoving the taller line can never help: the width shrinks and the height cannot grow past the shorter line.
LC 42Trapping Rain WaterHardBonus A · #141
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalTwo pointers with running maxima
Spot itWater trapped between bars after rain.
“Water above a bar = min(tallest left, tallest right) − bar. The smaller side's max is already final.”
class Solution {    public int trap(int[] height) {        int l = 0, r = height.length - 1, leftMax = 0, rightMax = 0, water = 0;        while (l < r) {            leftMax = Math.max(leftMax, height[l]);            rightMax = Math.max(rightMax, height[r]);            if (leftMax < rightMax) water += leftMax - height[l++];      // left side is decided            else water += rightMax - height[r--];                        // right side is decided        }        return water;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapMove the side whose max is SMALLER; that side's water is decided.
Variations
Prefix-max arrays version (easier to get right under pressure)
Two arrays: tallest bar up to i from the left, and from the right. Water at i is the smaller one minus the bar.
public int trap(int[] height) {    int n = height.length, water = 0;    int[] left = new int[n], right = new int[n];    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) left[i] = Math.max(i > 0 ? left[i - 1] : 0, height[i]);    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) right[i] = Math.max(i + 1 < n ? right[i + 1] : 0, height[i]);    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) water += Math.min(left[i], right[i]) - height[i];    return water;}
LC 33Search in Rotated Sorted ArrayMediumBonus A · #142
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalBinary search · one half is always sorted
Spot itFind a target in a sorted array that was rotated (distinct values).
“One half of [lo, hi] is sorted; if the target is inside that half go there, otherwise go to the other half.”
class Solution {    public int search(int[] nums, int target) {        int lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;        while (lo <= hi) {            int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;            if (nums[mid] == target) return mid;            if (nums[lo] <= nums[mid]) {                                       // left half sorted                if (nums[lo] <= target && target < nums[mid]) hi = mid - 1;                else lo = mid + 1;            } else {                                                           // right half sorted                if (nums[mid] < target && target <= nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1;                else hi = mid - 1;            }        }        return -1;    }}
CostO(log n) time · O(1) space
TrapUse nums[lo] <= nums[mid] (with =) to detect a sorted left half when lo == mid.
Variations
LC 153 · Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
Compare with the RIGHT end: if nums[mid] > nums[hi] the minimum is to the right of mid.
public int findMin(int[] nums) {    int lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;    while (lo < hi) {        int mid = (lo + hi) >>> 1;        if (nums[mid] > nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;    }    return nums[lo];}
LC 55Jump GameMediumBonus A · #143
learn Sun 29Mon 30Wed 2finalGreedy reach
Spot itFrom each index you may jump up to nums[i]; can you reach the end?
“Keep the farthest reachable index; if you ever stand beyond it, you are stuck.”
class Solution {    public boolean canJump(int[] nums) {        int reach = 0;        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {            if (i > reach) return false;            reach = Math.max(reach, i + nums[i]);        }        return true;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapCheck i > reach BEFORE using nums[i].
Variations
LC 45 · Jump Game II (fewest jumps)
BFS by levels without a queue: end is the edge of the current level, far the edge of the next one.
public int jump(int[] nums) {    int jumps = 0, end = 0, far = 0;    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length - 1; i++) {        far = Math.max(far, i + nums[i]);        if (i == end) { jumps++; end = far; }            // leave the current level    }    return jumps;}

LC 5Longest Palindromic SubstringMediumBonus B · #144
learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3finalExpand around centres
Spot itThe longest contiguous palindrome inside s.
“Every palindrome has a centre: a letter or a gap. Grow from all 2n − 1 centres.”
class Solution {    public String longestPalindrome(String s) {        int bestL = 0, bestLen = 0;        for (int c = 0; c < 2 * s.length() - 1; c++) {            int l = c / 2, r = l + c % 2;                                    // letter or gap centre            while (l >= 0 && r < s.length() && s.charAt(l) == s.charAt(r)) { l--; r++; }            if (r - l - 1 > bestLen) { bestLen = r - l - 1; bestL = l + 1; }  // one step too far        }        return s.substring(bestL, bestL + bestLen);    }}
CostO(n²) time · O(1) space
TrapAfter the while loop the palindrome is s[l+1 .. r−1]: the last step went one too far.
Variations

learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3finalGrid DP
Spot itPaths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down.
“Ways into a cell = ways from above + ways from the left.”
class Solution {    public int uniquePaths(int m, int n) {        int[] dp = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(dp, 1);                                  // first row: one way each        for (int i = 1; i < m; i++)            for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) dp[j] += dp[j - 1];  // above + left        return dp[n - 1];    }}
CostO(m·n) time · O(n) space

Math.min(dp[j], dp[j - 1]) : dp[j]);    return dp[n - 1];}
LC 309Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with CooldownMediumBonus B · #147
learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3finalState machine DP
Spot itBuy and sell many times, but after selling you must rest one day.
“Three states each day: holding, just sold, resting; move between them.”
class Solution {    public int maxProfit(int[] prices) {        int hold = Integer.MIN_VALUE / 2, sold = 0, rest = 0;        for (int p : prices) {            int h = hold, s = sold, r = rest;            hold = Math.max(h, r - p);                       // keep holding, or buy after resting            sold = h + p;                                    // sell today            rest = Math.max(r, s);                           // rest (cooldown ends)        }        return Math.max(sold, rest);    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapCompute the new values from YESTERDAY's three values (save them first).
Variations
  • LC 121 (one trade) — best = max(best, price − minSoFar).
  • LC 122 (unlimited, no cooldown) — Add every positive day-to-day rise.
  • LC 714 (with a fee) — Two states: hold = max(hold, cash − p), cash = max(cash, hold + p − fee).
LC 1235Maximum Profit in Job SchedulingHardBonus B · #148
learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3finalWeighted interval scheduling (DP + binary search)
Spot itNon-overlapping jobs with profits; maximise the total.
“Sort by end. Best up to job i = max(skip it, its profit + best of jobs ending by its start).”
class Solution {    public int jobScheduling(int[] startTime, int[] endTime, int[] profit) {        int n = startTime.length;        int[][] jobs = new int[n][];        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) jobs[i] = new int[]{startTime[i], endTime[i], profit[i]};        Arrays.sort(jobs, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));               // by end        int[] dp = new int[n + 1];                                              // dp[i] = best using the first i jobs        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {            int start = jobs[i - 1][0], lo = 0, hi = i - 1;                     // count jobs with end <= start            while (lo < hi) {                int mid = (lo + hi + 1) >>> 1;                if (jobs[mid - 1][1] <= start) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;            }            dp[i] = Math.max(dp[i - 1], dp[lo] + jobs[i - 1][2]);               // skip or take        }        return dp[n];    }}
CostO(n log n) time · O(n) space
TrapA job may start exactly when another ends: search for the last end <= start.
LC 91Decode WaysMediumBonus B · #149
learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3final1-D DP · one or two characters
Spot itCount ways to decode a digit string where 1..26 map to letters.
“Take one digit (if not '0') or two digits (if 10..26).”
class Solution {    public int numDecodings(String s) {        int prev2 = 1, prev1 = s.charAt(0) == '0' ? 0 : 1;           // ways for "" and for s[0]        for (int i = 1; i < s.length(); i++) {            int cur = 0;            if (s.charAt(i) != '0') cur += prev1;                     // one digit            int two = (s.charAt(i - 1) - '0') * 10 + (s.charAt(i) - '0');            if (two >= 10 && two <= 26) cur += prev2;                 // two digits            prev2 = prev1;            prev1 = cur;        }        return prev1;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapA '0' cannot stand alone: "06" has 0 ways.
LC 152Maximum Product SubarrayMediumBonus B · #150
learn Mon 30Tue 1Thu 3finalKadane with max and min
Spot itLargest product of a contiguous subarray (negatives and zeros allowed).
“A negative number turns the smallest product into the largest, so carry both.”
class Solution {    public int maxProduct(int[] nums) {        int hi = nums[0], lo = nums[0], best = nums[0];        for (int i = 1; i < nums.length; i++) {            int x = nums[i], h = hi;            hi = Math.max(x, Math.max(h * x, lo * x));            lo = Math.min(x, Math.min(h * x, lo * x));            best = Math.max(best, hi);        }        return best;    }}
CostO(n) time · O(1) space
TrapCompute the new max and min from the OLD pair (save one first).

Spot itget / put in O(1); when full, throw out the least recently used key.
“The map finds the node; the list keeps the order: newest after head, oldest before tail.”
class LRUCache {    private static final class Node {        int key, val;        Node prev, next;        Node(int k, int v) { key = k; val = v; }    }​    private final int capacity;    private final Map<Integer, Node> map = new HashMap<>();    private final Node head = new Node(0, 0), tail = new Node(0, 0);   // dummies​    public LRUCache(int capacity) {        this.capacity = capacity;        head.next = tail;        tail.prev = head;    }​    public int get(int key) {        Node node = map.get(key);        if (node == null) return -1;        unlink(node);        addFront(node);                                      // used: now the newest        return node.val;    }​    public void put(int key, int value) {        Node node = map.get(key);        if (node != null) { node.val = value; unlink(node); addFront(node); return; }        if (map.size() == capacity) {            Node old = tail.prev;                            // least recently used            unlink(old);            map.remove(old.key);        }        node = new Node(key, value);        map.put(key, node);        addFront(node);    }​    private void unlink(Node n) { n.prev.next = n.next; n.next.prev = n.prev; }​    private void addFront(Node n) {        n.next = head.next;        n.prev = head;        head.next.prev = n;        head.next = n;    }}
CostO(1) per operation · O(capacity) space
TrapOn get, move the node to the front too. Two dummy nodes (head, tail) remove every null check.
Variations
Short version with LinkedHashMap (say you know both)
accessOrder = true keeps entries in use order; removeEldestEntry evicts when the size passes capacity.
class LRUCache extends LinkedHashMap<Integer, Integer> {    private final int capacity;​    public LRUCache(int capacity) {        super(16, 0.75f, true);        this.capacity = capacity;    }​    public int get(int key) { return super.getOrDefault(key, -1); }​    public void put(int key, int value) { super.put(key, value); }​    @Override    protected boolean removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> eldest) { return size() > capacity; }}
LC 208Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)MediumBonus C · #152
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalTrie
Spot itinsert, search a whole word, and check whether any word starts with a prefix.
“One child per letter; a flag marks where a word ends.”
class Trie {    private final Trie[] next = new Trie[26];    private boolean end;​    public Trie() {}​    public void insert(String word) {        Trie node = this;        for (char c : word.toCharArray()) {            if (node.next[c - 'a'] == null) node.next[c - 'a'] = new Trie();            node = node.next[c - 'a'];        }        node.end = true;    }​    public boolean search(String word) {        Trie node = walk(word);        return node != null && node.end;    }​    public boolean startsWith(String prefix) {        return walk(prefix) != null;    }​    private Trie walk(String s) {        Trie node = this;        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {            node = node.next[c - 'a'];            if (node == null) return null;        }        return node;    }}
CostO(L) per operation · O(total letters) space
Trapsearch needs the end flag; startsWith does not.
Variations
LC 211 · Design Add and Search Words ('.' matches any letter)
The same trie; on '.', try every child with a small DFS.
class WordDictionary {    private final WordDictionary[] next = new WordDictionary[26];    private boolean end;​    public WordDictionary() {}​    public void addWord(String word) {        WordDictionary node = this;        for (char c : word.toCharArray()) {            if (node.next[c - 'a'] == null) node.next[c - 'a'] = new WordDictionary();            node = node.next[c - 'a'];        }        node.end = true;    }​    public boolean search(String word) { return find(word, 0, this); }​    private boolean find(String w, int i, WordDictionary node) {        if (i == w.length()) return node.end;        char c = w.charAt(i);        if (c != '.') return node.next[c - 'a'] != null && find(w, i + 1, node.next[c - 'a']);        for (WordDictionary child : node.next) if (child != null && find(w, i + 1, child)) return true;        return false;    }}
LC 295Find Median from Data StreamHardBonus C · #153
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalTwo heaps
Spot itAdd numbers one by one; report the median at any time.
“Max-heap holds the small half, min-heap the large half; keep sizes equal or the small half one bigger.”
class MedianFinder {    private final PriorityQueue<Integer> small = new PriorityQueue<>(Collections.reverseOrder());   // max-heap    private final PriorityQueue<Integer> large = new PriorityQueue<>();                            // min-heap​    public MedianFinder() {}​    public void addNum(int num) {        small.offer(num);        large.offer(small.poll());                                    // biggest of the small half moves up        if (large.size() > small.size()) small.offer(large.poll());   // rebalance    }​    public double findMedian() {        return small.size() > large.size() ? small.peek() : (small.peek() + (double) large.peek()) / 2;    }}
CostO(log n) add · O(1) median
TrapAlways pass the new number through one heap into the other, then rebalance; this keeps every small ≤ every large.
LC 23Merge k Sorted ListsHardBonus C · #154
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalMin-heap of list heads
Spot itMerge k sorted linked lists into one.
“The heap holds the current head of every list; pop the smallest, push its next.”
class Solution {    public ListNode mergeKLists(ListNode[] lists) {        PriorityQueue<ListNode> heap = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Integer.compare(a.val, b.val));        for (ListNode l : lists) if (l != null) heap.offer(l);        ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), tail = dummy;        while (!heap.isEmpty()) {            ListNode node = heap.poll();                                // smallest head            tail.next = node;            tail = node;            if (node.next != null) heap.offer(node.next);        }        return dummy.next;    }}
CostO(N log k) time · O(k) space
TrapSkip null lists when filling the heap.
Variations
LC 21 · Merge Two Sorted Lists
Dummy head and a tail pointer; attach the smaller node each time, then the rest.
public ListNode mergeTwoLists(ListNode list1, ListNode list2) {    ListNode dummy = new ListNode(0), tail = dummy;    while (list1 != null && list2 != null) {        if (list1.val <= list2.val) { tail.next = list1; list1 = list1.next; }        else { tail.next = list2; list2 = list2.next; }        tail = tail.next;    }    tail.next = list1 != null ? list1 : list2;    return dummy.next;}
LC 98Validate Binary Search TreeMediumBonus C · #155
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalRecursion with bounds
Spot itIs this binary tree a valid BST (strict)?
“Every node must lie strictly between the bounds its ancestors set.”
class Solution {    public boolean isValidBST(TreeNode root) {        return ok(root, Long.MIN_VALUE, Long.MAX_VALUE);    }​    private boolean ok(TreeNode n, long lo, long hi) {        if (n == null) return true;        if (n.val <= lo || n.val >= hi) return false;        return ok(n.left, lo, n.val) && ok(n.right, n.val, hi);        // left caps hi, right raises lo    }}
CostO(n) time · O(h) space
TrapChecking only parent vs child is wrong; and values can be Integer.MIN/MAX, so pass the bounds as long.
Variations
LC 230 · Kth Smallest Element in a BST
An in-order walk of a BST visits values in sorted order. Do it with a stack and stop at the k-th pop.
public int kthSmallest(TreeNode root, int k) {    Deque<TreeNode> st = new ArrayDeque<>();    TreeNode cur = root;    while (true) {        while (cur != null) { st.push(cur); cur = cur.left; }    // go as far left as possible        cur = st.pop();        if (--k == 0) return cur.val;        cur = cur.right;    }}
LC 1192Critical Connections in a NetworkHardBonus C · #156
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalBridges (Tarjan low-link)
Spot itEdges whose removal disconnects the graph.
“low[v] = earliest discovery time v's subtree can reach with one back edge. Edge (u, v) is a bridge if low[v] > tin[u].”
class Solution {    private List<List<Integer>> g;    private int[] tin, low;    private int timer;    private List<List<Integer>> bridges;​    public List<List<Integer>> criticalConnections(int n, List<List<Integer>> connections) {        g = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g.add(new ArrayList<>());        for (List<Integer> e : connections) { g.get(e.get(0)).add(e.get(1)); g.get(e.get(1)).add(e.get(0)); }        tin = new int[n];        low = new int[n];        Arrays.fill(tin, -1);        timer = 0;        bridges = new ArrayList<>();        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (tin[i] == -1) dfs(i, -1);        return bridges;    }​    private void dfs(int u, int parent) {        tin[u] = low[u] = timer++;        for (int w : g.get(u)) {            if (w == parent) continue;            if (tin[w] != -1) low[u] = Math.min(low[u], tin[w]);     // back edge            else {                dfs(w, u);                low[u] = Math.min(low[u], low[w]);                if (low[w] > tin[u]) bridges.add(List.of(u, w));     // w cannot climb past u            }        }    }}
CostO(V + E) time · O(V + E) space
TrapSkip only the edge back to the PARENT, and update low[u] with tin[w] for back edges.
Variations
  • Articulation points — A non-root u is a cut vertex if some child v has low[v] >= tin[u]; the root if it has 2+ children.
LC 79Word SearchMediumBonus C · #157
learn Tue 1Wed 2Fri 4finalGrid backtracking
Spot itDoes the word appear as a path of adjacent cells, each cell used once?
“Try every start; mark the cell, explore 4 ways, unmark on the way back.”
class Solution {    public boolean exist(char[][] board, String word) {        for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++)            for (int j = 0; j < board[0].length; j++)                if (dfs(board, word, 0, i, j)) return true;        return false;    }​    private boolean dfs(char[][] b, String w, int k, int r, int c) {        if (k == w.length()) return true;        if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= b.length || c >= b[0].length || b[r][c] != w.charAt(k)) return false;        char saved = b[r][c];        b[r][c] = '#';                                                               // mark        boolean found = dfs(b, w, k + 1, r + 1, c) || dfs(b, w, k + 1, r - 1, c)                     || dfs(b, w, k + 1, r, c + 1) || dfs(b, w, k + 1, r, c - 1);        b[r][c] = saved;                                                             // unmark        return found;    }}
CostO(m·n·3^L) time · O(L) space
TrapRestore the cell after exploring, or other start points see a damaged board.
